definition_zh: 愚蠢的；愚钝可笑的；驴一般的
definition_en: extremely stupid or silly
core_image: 对着一堵墙反复撞头的驴
scene: 他把密码设成了生日倒序，被朋友嘲笑这个主意实在不高明。 His asinine plan to cheat the test was caught within minutes.
sceneCN: 这里 asinine 是「愚蠢可笑的」（第 1 个义项：像驴一样愚蠢）；句意是他作弊的蠢计划几分钟内就被发现。

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「愚蠢地」
由形容词加名词后缀构成，义为「愚蠢；蠢话」
同源基础词，义为「驴；蠢人」

senses.title: Extremely stupid or silly
senses.definition: utterly senseless, foolish, or ridiculous
senses.definitionCN: 毫无头脑、愚蠢或可笑的
senses.example: It was asinine to drive without a license.
senses.exampleCN: 无证驾驶真是愚蠢至极。
senses.why: Latin asinus means donkey, an animal proverbially seen as stubborn and witless, so the adjective calls behavior donkey-like in its stupidity.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 asinus 意为驴，这种动物素以顽固迟钝著称，因此该形容词指行为像驴一样愚蠢。

senses.title: Of or like a donkey
senses.definition: relating to or resembling an ass or donkey
senses.definitionCN: 与驴相关或似驴的
senses.example: In zoology texts, asinine describes the donkey family.
senses.exampleCN: 在动物学文献中，asinine 描述驴科动物。
senses.why: The word keeps its literal animal sense in scientific contexts.
senses.whyCN: 在科学语境中，该词保留了字面的动物义。

intro.en: Asinine comes from Latin asinus, donkey, with the adjective suffix -inus.
intro.cn: asinine 源自拉丁语 asinus（驴），加形容词后缀 -inus 构成。

items.en: The root *as- may name the wild ass of ancient steppe lands; the origin is generally thought so but not certain.
items.cn: 词根 *as- 或指古代草原上的野驴；一般认为如此，但不确定。

items.en: Asinus meant donkey and, by extension, a dull person.
items.cn: 拉丁语 asinus 指驴，引申指迟钝的人。

items.en: Asininus meant donkey-like or foolish.
items.cn: 后期拉丁语 asininus 意为似驴的、愚蠢的。

items.en: Old French asin carried the word onward.
items.cn: 古法语 asin 使该词得以传承。

items.en: English adopted asinine in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 十七世纪英语借入 asinine。

note.en: The insult sense came first in spirit: calling someone a donkey was already Roman slang.
note.cn: 「蠢」义早有雏形：骂人像驴，在古罗马已是俚语。

abstract.cn: 想象一头耳朵贴平、拒绝前行的驴。

abstract.en: Hear the bray as the sound of nonsense.

abstract.en: See a lecture where every point is nonsense applauded.

examples.en: Canceling the meeting twice was simply asinine.
examples.cn: 两次取消会议简直是愚蠢可笑。

examples.en: The novel's narrator mocks his own asinine choices.

examples.en: Zoologists noted the asinine features of the hybrid.

definition_zh: 原型；典型；典型人物
definition_en: the original pattern or model from which copies are made; a perfect example of a type
core_image: 所有摹本都照着刻的第一块模子
scene: 雕塑工坊里，学徒们各自临摹着同一尊陶像。 The old statue is the archetype of the mother goddess.
sceneCN: 这里 archetype 是「原型、原始典范」（第 1 个义项：最初的模型）；句意是这尊古像是大地母神的最早原型。

collocations.zh: 荣格所说的原型（集体无意识中的原始意象）

derivatives.zh: archetype 加形容词后缀 -al，义为「典型的、原型的」
type 加前缀 stereo-（固定），义为「刻板印象」，与原型相对
type 加前缀 proto-（最初），义为「样机、雏形」
type 派生动词，义为「作为……的典型」

senses.title: The original model of a kind
senses.definition: the very first form of something from which later copies or versions derive
senses.definitionCN: 某类事物的最初形态，后来的摹本或版本皆由此衍生
senses.example: The clay tablet is the archetype of all later printed calendars.
senses.exampleCN: 这块泥版是后世各种印制历书的原型。
senses.why: Arkhos means first in rank, so the archetype stands first in a line of copies.
senses.whyCN: arkhos 意为「居首」，原型即处于一列摹本之首。

senses.title: A perfect typical example
senses.definition: someone or something that shows the essential features of a class in the purest form
senses.definitionCN: 以最纯粹形式体现某类事物本质特征的人或物
senses.example: Sherlock Holmes became the archetype of the private detective.
senses.exampleCN: 夏洛克·福尔摩斯成了私家侦探的典型。
senses.why: If the first model defines the class, the best exemplar embodies that definition.
senses.whyCN: 最初的模型定义了一类事物，最完美的实例便体现这一定义。

senses.title: An inherited mental image in psychology
senses.definition: in Jungian theory, an ancient universal image or pattern in the collective unconscious
senses.definitionCN: 荣格理论中集体无意识里古老的普遍意象或模式
senses.example: The wise old man is one of Jung's best-known archetypes.
senses.exampleCN: 「智慧老人」是荣格最著名的原型之一。
senses.why: Primordial first-images stored in the mind parallel first-models in the world.
senses.whyCN: 心中储存的原始「首像」与世上的「首模」彼此平行。

senses.title: A recurrent symbolic pattern in literature
senses.definition: a recurring character, plot or symbol type found across many stories and cultures
senses.definitionCN: 在不同故事与文化中反复出现的角色、情节或象征类型
senses.example: The hero's journey is the most familiar archetype in world folklore.
senses.exampleCN: 「英雄之旅」是世界民间故事中最常见的原型模式。
senses.why: Stories repeat first-patterns, just as crafts copy first-models.
senses.whyCN: 故事重复最初的母题，正如工匠复制最初的模型。

senses.title: The Platonic ideal form
senses.definition: in Platonic philosophy, the eternal ideal of which earthly things are imperfect copies
senses.definitionCN: 柏拉图哲学中永恒的理想型，世间万物皆是其不完善的摹本
senses.example: For Plato, every table imitates the archetype of the table.
senses.exampleCN: 柏拉图认为，每一张桌子都模仿「桌子」的理念原型。
senses.why: Plato's eternal forms are the philosophical ancestors of the first-model image.
senses.whyCN: 柏拉图的水恒理式正是「最初模型」这一意象的哲学源头。

intro.en: Archetype joins the Greek prefix arkh- (chief, first) with typos (blow, mold, pattern).
intro.cn: archetype 由希腊语前缀 arkh-（首要）与 typos（打击、铸模、样式）复合而成。

items.en: The root *terk- gave Greek arkhein, to begin or rule.
items.cn: 词根 *terk- 衍生出希腊语 arkhein，义为「开始；统治」（重构形式）。

items.en: Arkhetupon meant pattern, model, literally first-molded.
items.cn: 希腊语 arkhetupon 意为「范型、模型」，字面即「首先铸成的」。

items.en: Latin borrowed the word as archetypum, keeping the sense of original pattern.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入该词作 archetypum，保留「原始范型」之义。

items.en: Neoplatonist writers used archetype for the eternal ideas behind visible things.
items.cn: 新柏拉图主义作者用 archetype 指可见事物背后的永恒理念。

items.en: The word entered English through learned Latin, first in philosophical contexts.
items.cn: 该词经学术拉丁语进入英语，最初用于哲学语境。

items.en: Jung's psychology made archetype a household term for universal mental patterns.
items.cn: 荣格心理学使 archetype 成为描述普遍心理模式的常用术语。

note.en: Three type-words divide the field: first model, earliest prototype, and fixed cliché.
note.cn: 三个 type 系单词分工明确：原型、最早样机、刻板印象。

normal.en: archi- = chief, first; type = mold: the first mold.
normal.cn: archi- 表「首要」，type 表「模子」：第一块模子。

normal.en: Compare prototype: proto- (first) + type = early working model.
normal.cn: 对比 prototype：proto-（最初）+ type = 早期样机。

normal.en: archetypal is the adjective: an archetypal villain.
normal.cn: 形容词是 archetypal：一个「最典型」的反派。

normal.en: In Jungian psychology, archetypes are shared mental images.
normal.cn: 在荣格心理学中，原型是全人类共有的心理意象。

normal.en: The hero, the mother, the trickster are classic archetypes.
normal.cn: 英雄、母亲、捣蛋鬼都是经典原型。

abstract.en: Picture the first wooden horse mold, every later toy horse copied from it.
abstract.cn: 想象第一只木马模子，后来所有玩具马都照它复制。

abstract.en: See a spotlight on one figure who sums up every hero ever written.
abstract.cn: 想象聚光灯照在一个身影上，他概括了史上所有英雄。

abstract.en: Feel the arch of an ancient temple gate holding the first carved image.
abstract.cn: 感受古庙拱门托起第一尊刻像的画面。

examples.en: The film offers the archetype of the lonely cowboy.
examples.cn: 这部电影塑造了孤独牛仔的典型形象。

examples.en: Her workshop produced the archetype of the modern office chair.
examples.cn: 她的工作室造出了现代办公椅的原型。

examples.en: Scholars trace the archetype of the flood story to ancient Mesopotamia.
examples.cn: 学者们把洪水故事的最初母题追溯到古代美索不达米亚。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿琪·太普」——阿琪太爱拍照（typo 的姊妹 type），她的姿势成了全班模仿的原型。

sensesIntro.en: From the first mold to perfect exemplar, shared mental image, literary pattern and Platonic ideal.
sensesIntro.cn: 由「第一块模子」延伸到完美典范、共有心理意象、文学母题与柏拉图理念。

latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语借入 typos 作 typus，由此衍生出罗曼语与英语词汇。

definition_zh: 和睦；友好关系；亲善
definition_en: a friendly, peaceful relationship between people, groups, or nations
core_image: 握手后的和平：曾经的对手坐上了同一张桌子
scene: 停战协议签订后，两国边境市场重新热闹起来。 The treaty restored amity between the two bordering nations.
sceneCN: 这里的 amity 是「和睦、友好关系」（第 1 个义项：国家或群体间的和平友好）；句意是条约恢复了两个邻国之间的和睦关系。

derivatives.zh: 同根形容词，义为「友好的；心平气和的」，形容关系与解决方式
同根形容词，义为「和蔼可亲的」，形容个人性情
amicable 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「友好地；心平气和地」

senses.title: Peaceful relations between groups or nations
senses.titleCN: 国家群体间的和睦友好
senses.definition: a state of friendship and peace between countries, organizations, or communities
senses.definitionCN: 国家、组织或社区之间的友好和平状态
senses.example: Centuries of amity followed the marriage alliance.
senses.exampleCN: 联姻结盟之后是几个世纪的睦邻友好。
senses.why: From Latin amicus, friend: nations that treat each other as friends live without war.
senses.whyCN: 源自拉丁语 amicus「朋友」：把彼此当朋友的国家便无战事。

senses.title: Harmony among individuals
senses.definition: friendly accord between individual persons, especially former opponents
senses.definitionCN: 个人之间的友好一致，尤其指昔日的对手之间
senses.example: The old rivals retired to the bar in complete amity.
senses.exampleCN: 这对老对手赛后一起去酒吧，相处融洽。
senses.why: The friend-image scales down from nations to any pair of people.
senses.whyCN: 「朋友」意象可以从国家缩小到任意两个人之间。

senses.title: Formal friendship sealed by agreement
senses.definition: friendship declared or guaranteed in a formal document, as in treaties of amity
senses.definitionCN: 见于正式文件、被宣告或保障的友好，如友好条约
senses.example: The two republics signed a treaty of amity and commerce.
senses.exampleCN: 两个共和国签署了友好通商条约。
senses.why: Diplomacy needed a dignified noun for friendship, and amity supplied it.
senses.whyCN: 外交需要一个庄重的名词来表示「友谊」，amity 正好承担此职。

senses.title: Goodwill and cooperation without hostility
senses.definition: an attitude of goodwill that keeps cooperation free of antagonism
senses.definitionCN: 使合作免于敌对的善意态度
senses.example: The merger talks proceeded in an atmosphere of amity.
senses.exampleCN: 并购谈判在友好的气氛中进行。
senses.why: Friendship is not only a status but a spirit that shapes how business is done.
senses.whyCN: 友谊不仅是状态，更是一种塑造做事方式的精神。

senses.title: Concord within a community or family
senses.definition: peace and accord within a household, sect, or small community
senses.definitionCN: 家庭、教派或小团体内部的和平一致
senses.example: Family amity survived even the quarrel over the will.
senses.exampleCN: 即使为遗嘱争吵，家人依旧和睦。
senses.why: The smallest 'nation' is the family, and friendship scales all the way down.
senses.whyCN: 最小的「国」是家，「朋友」意象可以一路缩到家门之内。

intro.en: Amity comes from Latin amicus, friend, through Old French amitie, meaning friendship.
intro.cn: amity 源自拉丁语 amicus「朋友」，经古法语 amitie（友谊）进入英语。

items.en: Root *am-, to love or be attached.
items.cn: 原始印欧语词根 *am-「爱、依恋」。

items.en: amicus, friend; amicitia, friendship.
items.cn: 拉丁语 amicus「朋友」；amicitia「友谊」。

items.en: amitie, friendship, borrowed from Latin amicitia.
items.cn: 古法语 amitie「友谊」，借自拉丁语 amicitia。

items.en: English amity appears in diplomatic and moral writing for peaceful accord.
items.cn: 十五世纪英语 amity 出现于外交与道德文字，指和平和睦。

items.en: Treaties of amity became a fixed formula in European statecraft.
items.cn: 「友好条约」成为欧洲国家交往的固定用语。

items.en: Now a formal or literary word for harmony between peoples or persons.
items.cn: 如今是表示民族或人际和谐的书卷用语。

note.en: Keep amity apart from its sibling amiable and from near rivals for peace and friendship.
note.cn: 把 amity 与同根词 amiable 区分开，并与其他表示和平友谊的近义词对比。

entries.definition: adjective for a lovable person; amity is the noun for the resulting harmony.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，形容人可爱和蔼；amity 是由此产生的和睦关系名词。

entries.definition: adjective for relations settled without conflict, as an amicable divorce.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，形容关系无冲突地解决，如友好离婚。

entries.definition: active hostility; from Latin inimicus, not-a-friend — the mirror opposite of amity.

entries.definition: agreement and harmony, often within a group.

entries.definition: pleasing agreement in general, musical or social.
entries.definitionCN: 和谐；泛指协调一致，可用于音乐或人际关系。

entries.definition: benevolent attitude; the inner disposition behind amity.

normal.en: Family chain: amare → amicus → amity, amiable, amicable.

normal.en: a-MITY rhymes with community — communities need amity.

abstract.en: Picture former rivals sharing one umbrella in the rain.
abstract.cn: 想象昔日的对手在雨里共撑一把伞。

abstract.en: Amity sounds like 'amity and light' — picture a border village lit in peace.

examples.en: The festival was founded to promote amity among the immigrant communities.

examples.en: After decades of hostility, the neighbors finally lived in amity.

examples.en: The summit closed with a declaration of amity and cooperation.

definition_zh: 风速；空气流动的速度；风速等级；设计风速；风速预报值
definition_en: the rate at which air moves past a point, usually measured in metres per second or knots
core_image: 风杯转速仪在桅杆顶端飞快旋转，表盘上的数字不断向上跳动

sceneCN: 这里 wind speed 指「空气经过某一点时的移动速率」（第 1 个义项：可用仪器测出的基本风速）；句意为桅杆处的风速从中午起已经翻倍。图中可辨识物件：桅杆、风杯、读数表盘、记录本。

senses.title: The measured rate of air movement
senses.definition: the distance air travels past a point in a given unit of time
senses.definitionCN: 单位时间内空气经过某一点所走的距离
senses.example: The tower recorded a wind speed of fifteen metres per second.
senses.exampleCN: 塔台记录到的风速是每秒十五米。
senses.why: The compound simply names the speed of the wind, just as water speed names the speed of water.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词就是「风的速度」，正如 water speed 指水的速度。

senses.title: Units and instruments
senses.titleCN: 风速的计量单位与仪器
senses.definition: the scales and devices, such as knots, metres per second and anemometers, used to express wind speed
senses.definitionCN: 用来表示风速的单位与装置，如节、米每秒与风速计
senses.example: Sailors still quote wind speed in knots on the bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 水手在驾驶台上仍用节来表示风速。
senses.why: Once a quantity is measured regularly, its units and instruments are discussed under the same name.
senses.whyCN: 一个量一旦被常规测量，它的单位与仪器也会用同一个名称来讨论。

senses.title: A step on the Beaufort scale
senses.definition: one of the numbered categories that describe the effects of a given wind speed
senses.definitionCN: 按给定风速描述其影响的分级编号之一
senses.example: At that wind speed the sea builds whitecaps offshore.
senses.exampleCN: 在这样的风速下，近海会起白浪。
senses.why: The scale converts a numerical speed into an observable category, but the category is still spoken of as a wind speed.
senses.whyCN: 风级把数字化的速度转换成可观察的类别，但人们仍以风速来称呼这个类别。

senses.title: A design load for structures
senses.definition: the wind speed a building, bridge or tower is engineered to withstand
senses.definitionCN: 建筑、桥梁或塔架按设计需要承受的风速
senses.example: The code sets a design wind speed for every coastal district.
senses.exampleCN: 规范为每个沿海地区规定了设计风速。
senses.why: Engineering turns the measured quantity into a load, and keeps the same name for the design value.
senses.whyCN: 工程把测得的值变成荷载，而设计值仍沿用同一个名称。

senses.title: Rated speed for a wind turbine
senses.titleCN: 风力发电机的额定风速
senses.definition: the wind speed at which a turbine reaches its stated power output
senses.definitionCN: 涡轮机达到标称输出功率时的风速
senses.example: Below the rated wind speed the turbine produces less than its maximum.
senses.exampleCN: 低于额定风速时，涡轮机的发电量达不到最大值。
senses.why: The energy industry needs a fixed reference point, so it names that point by the wind speed itself.
senses.whyCN: 能源行业需要一个固定参照点，于是直接用风速来命名该点。

senses.title: An operating limit for aircraft and ships
senses.titleCN: 航空与航海的操作风速限制
senses.definition: the maximum wind speed at which a landing, take-off or manoeuvre is considered safe
senses.definitionCN: 着陆、起飞或操作被认为安全所允许的最大风速
senses.example: The flight was delayed because the wind speed exceeded the crosswind limit.
senses.exampleCN: 因为风速超过了侧风限值，航班延误了。
senses.why: Operators work with thresholds, and the threshold is naturally described as a wind speed.
senses.whyCN: 操作者依据阈值行事，而阈值自然就以风速来描述。

senses.title: Change of speed with height
senses.definition: the increase or decrease in wind speed between one level and another, as in wind shear
senses.definitionCN: 不同高度之间风速的增减，如风切变
senses.example: Pilots watch for a sharp change in wind speed near the runway.
senses.exampleCN: 飞行员会留意跑道附近风速的急剧变化。
senses.why: The quantity is compared between two heights, so the phrase appears in the study of gradients and shear.
senses.whyCN: 这个量在两个高度之间作比较，因此该短语出现在梯度与切变研究中。

senses.title: A forecast value
senses.definition: the wind speed predicted for a place and time in a weather forecast
senses.definitionCN: 天气预报中为某地某时预测的风速
senses.example: The evening forecast raised the expected wind speed to forty knots.
senses.exampleCN: 晚间预报把预计风速提高到四十节。
senses.why: Forecasting is about the future value of the same measured quantity, so no new term is needed.
senses.whyCN: 预报说的是同一个被测量在未来的数值，因此不需要新术语。

intro.en: Wind speed is an English compound of two native words. Wind goes back to Old English wind, and speed to Old English spēd, which first meant 'success, prosperity' before it came to mean 'rate of motion'.
intro.cn: wind speed 是两个英语本族词构成的复合短语。wind 上溯古英语 wind；speed 上溯古英语 spēd，原义为「成功、兴旺」，后来才表示「运动速率」。

items.en: Wind meant moving air and belongs to the same Germanic stock as Dutch wind and German Wind.
items.cn: wind 意为流动的空气，与荷兰语 wind、德语 Wind 同属日耳曼语族。

items.en: Spēd meant 'success, good fortune, quickness', with a related verb spōwan 'to prosper'.
items.cn: spēd 意为「成功、好运、迅速」，并有相关动词 spōwan「兴旺」。

items.en: During the Middle English period speed narrowed from 'success' to 'swiftness' and then to 'rate of motion', which is the sense used in the compound.
items.cn: 在中古英语时期，speed 从「成功」收窄为「迅速」，再变为「运动速率」，也就是复合词所用的义项。

items.en: Wind speed became a standard item in nineteenth-century weather records, once anemometers were read regularly at stations.
items.cn: 随着测站开始常规读取风速计，wind speed 在 19 世纪的天气记录中成为标准项目。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date only): no exact first citation for the compound is fixed, and the speed word's shift from 'success' has no single recorded date.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代）：这个复合词没有确切的最早书证，speed 从「成功」转为「速率」也没有单一可考的日期。

note.en: Group one holds speed compounds that are easily confused with wind speed; group two holds other ways of naming how fast air or a craft moves.
note.cn: 第一组是容易与 wind speed 混淆的速度复合词；第二组是表示空气或飞行器运动快慢的其他说法。

entries.definition: The speed of an aircraft relative to the surrounding air, not the speed of the air itself.
entries.definitionCN: 飞机相对周围空气的速度，而不是空气本身的速度。

entries.definition: The speed of an aircraft relative to the ground, which differs from both airspeed and wind speed.
entries.definitionCN: 飞机相对地面的速度，与空速和风速都不同。

entries.definition: The compass direction from which the wind blows, paired with wind speed in every weather report.
entries.definitionCN: 风吹来的方位，在每份天气报告中与风速并列。

entries.definition: The peak speed of a brief blast, often higher than the steady wind speed.
entries.definitionCN: 一阵短促强风的峰值速度，通常高于稳定风速。

entries.definition: Speed in a stated direction; wind velocity includes both the rate and the direction of the air.
entries.definitionCN: 带方向的速度；风的 velocity 同时包含速率与方向。

entries.definition: The strength of the wind expressed as a force or Beaufort number rather than a measured rate.
entries.definitionCN: 以力或蒲福风级表示的风的强度，而非测得的速率。

entries.definition: A technical term for the speed of air in a duct or around an object, often used in engineering.
entries.definitionCN: 指管道内或物体周围空气速度的技术术语，常用于工程。

entries.definition: The rate at which sound travels through a medium, a fixed property rather than a local wind condition.
entries.definitionCN: 声音在介质中传播的速率，是固定属性，而非某地的风况。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: two real native roots, real units and real weather collocations, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：两个真实的英语本族词根、真实单位与真实天气搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: wind + speed: literally the speed of the wind, a transparent compound.
normal.cn: wind + speed：字面就是风的速度，构词完全透明。

normal.en: Speed once meant 'success'; the modern sense of rate grew out of the idea of getting on quickly.
normal.cn: speed 原义为「成功」；现代速率义从「事情进展得快」这一想法长出。

normal.en: Weather reports always pair wind speed with wind direction.
normal.cn: 天气报告总把风速与风向并列。

normal.en: Units are part of the term: metres per second, knots, kilometres per hour.
normal.cn: 单位是术语的一部分：米每秒、节、公里每小时。

normal.en: The anemometer is the instrument that turns wind speed into a reading.
normal.cn: 风速计是把风速变成读数的仪器。

abstract.en: Picture three cups spinning on a pole, each turn counted by a quiet meter.
abstract.cn: 想象杆顶三只风杯旋转，每一圈都被一台安静的仪表记下。

abstract.en: Picture a flag that stiffens from limp to straight as the number climbs.
abstract.cn: 想象旗子随数字上升，从垂软变得笔直。

abstract.en: Picture a turbine that begins to produce power only after the air reaches one fixed rate.
abstract.cn: 想象风机只有在空气达到某个固定速率后才开始发电。

examples.en: The anemometer logged a peak wind speed just before the squall.
examples.cn: 风速计在飑线到来前记录到峰值风速。

examples.en: Engineers tested the bridge model at twice the design wind speed.
examples.cn: 工程师用两倍设计风速测试了桥梁模型。

examples.en: The forecast warned of a wind speed that could ground small boats.
examples.cn: 预报警告风速可能让小船无法出航。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「风快」——风跑得有多快，就是风速

root: 复合短语：wind 来自古英语 wind，属日耳曼语族；speed 来自古英语 spēd「成功、兴旺」，中古英语时期转为「迅速、速率」。气象义在 19 世纪风速计常规观测后成为标准项目，确切最早书证不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one line: the rate of moving air is measured, then expressed in units, graded, designed for, harvested, limited, compared between heights and finally forecast.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一条线索展开：流动空气的速率先被测量，再以单位表达、分级、用于设计、用于发电、设为限值、在不同高度比较，最后进入预报。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: three spinning cups on a mast, their turns counted into a number.
core.cn: 核心意象：桅杆上三只旋转的风杯，转数被折算成一个数字。

branches.en: MEASURE AND UNITS: a quantity is only useful once its scale is fixed.
branches.cn: 测量与单位：一个量只有定好标尺才有用。

branches.en: OBSERVABLE GRADE: the Beaufort step turns a number into a visible sea state.
branches.cn: 可观察的等级：蒲福风级把数字变成可见的海况。

branches.en: SAFETY THRESHOLDS: buildings and aircraft are both designed against a stated speed.
branches.cn: 安全阈值：建筑与飞机都按某一给定风速来设计。

branches.en: ENERGY REFERENCE: a turbine's output is pinned to one rated speed.
branches.cn: 能量参照：风机的输出被钉在一个额定风速上。

branches.en: COMPARISON AND PREDICTION: speed is compared between heights and projected into the future.
branches.cn: 比较与预测：风速在不同高度间比较，并被投射到未来。

intro.en: The phrase joins two free roots, and each root has its own suffix family: speed gives speedy and speedometer, while wind gives windy and windless.
intro.cn: 这个短语连接两个自由词根，各自有后缀词族：speed 给出 speedy 与 speedometer，wind 给出 windy 与 windless。

latinIntro.en: The compound is fully English, so there is no Latin term behind it. Latin ventus is only a cognate of the wind half, and spēs is not related to speed at all.
latinIntro.cn: 这个复合词完全是英语构成，背后没有拉丁术语。拉丁语 ventus 只是 wind 那一半的同源词，而 spēs 与 speed 毫无关系。

senses.title: A person who writes code
senses.definition: someone whose work is to write and correct the instructions a computer runs
senses.definitionCN: 以编写与修正计算机所执行指令为工作的人
senses.example: The programmer traced the fault to a single line of code.
senses.exampleCN: 这位程序员把故障追到一行代码上。
senses.why: the agent ending -er on the base program gives the plainest sense: the one who writes the program.
senses.whyCN: 词基 program 加施事词尾 -er，最直接的意思就是写程序的人。

senses.title: A software professional
senses.definition: a job title for someone employed to build and maintain software in a team
senses.definitionCN: 在团队中被雇来构建与维护软件的职业头衔
senses.example: The company hired ten programmers for the new app.
senses.exampleCN: 公司为这款新应用雇了十名程序员。
senses.why: the craft became an industry job, and the simple agent noun became a payroll category.
senses.whyCN: 这门手艺成了行业岗位，简单的施事名词也成了工资表上的类别。

senses.title: One who plans an event programme
senses.definition: the person who decides which acts, films or talks appear and in what order
senses.definitionCN: 决定哪些节目、影片或报告出现及其顺序的人
senses.example: The festival programmer chose films from thirty countries.
senses.exampleCN: 音乐节的节目编排者选了三十个国家的影片。
senses.why: this is the older sense: a programmer programs a season by deciding its running order, with no computer involved.
senses.whyCN: 这是较早的词义：编排者通过决定演出顺序来编排一个演出季，不涉及计算机。

senses.title: One who sets a device
senses.definition: a person who enters times and conditions into a timer or control unit
senses.definitionCN: 把时间与条件输入定时器或控制单元的人
senses.example: The heating programmer came to set the boiler for winter.
senses.exampleCN: 供暖设定员来把锅炉调成冬季模式。
senses.why: when the task is only to load a small sequence into a household device, the agent noun still fits.
senses.whyCN: 当任务只是往家用设备里装入一小段序列时，这个施事名词依然适用。

senses.title: A channel schedule planner
senses.definition: a broadcast professional who chooses what a station airs and when
senses.definitionCN: 决定电台或电视台播什么、何时播的广播从业者
senses.example: As a channel programmer, she decides what airs on Fridays.
senses.exampleCN: 作为频道编排者，她决定周五播什么。
senses.why: broadcasting kept the scheduling sense and turned it into a distinct job title.
senses.whyCN: 广播保留了「排顺序」义，并把它变成一个独立职位。

senses.title: A systems-level specialist
senses.definition: someone who works close to the operating system, drivers or hardware interfaces
senses.definitionCN: 在操作系统、驱动或硬件接口附近工作的人
senses.example: The systems programmer rewrote the device driver in assembly.
senses.exampleCN: 系统程序员用汇编重写了设备驱动。
senses.why: once software split into layers, the same title gained a prefix that marks how deep the work goes.
senses.whyCN: 软件一旦分层，同一个头衔就加上前缀，标明工作深入到哪一层。

senses.title: One who programs industrial machines
senses.definition: a technician who writes control sequences for machine tools or production equipment
senses.definitionCN: 为机床或生产设备编写控制序列的技术人员
senses.example: The shop hired a control programmer for its new lathe.
senses.exampleCN: 车间为新机床雇了一名控制编程员。
senses.why: the machine need not be a computer; a written sequence of movements is enough to make the title apply.
senses.whyCN: 机器不必是计算机，只要有一份写好的动作序列，这个头衔就成立。

senses.title: A statistical programmer
senses.definition: a specialist who writes analysis code for clinical trials or large studies
senses.definitionCN: 为临床试验或大型研究编写分析代码的专职人员
senses.example: The statistical programmer prepared the tables for the trial report.
senses.exampleCN: 统计程序员为试验报告准备了表格。
senses.why: fields that depend on repeated analysis gave the general title a domain adjective and a fixed role.
senses.whyCN: 依赖重复分析的领域给这个通用头衔加上领域形容词，形成固定岗位。

intro.en: Programmer is program plus the native agent ending -er. Its event-planning sense is nineteenth-century; the computing sense arrived with electronic machines in the 1940s. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: programmer 是 program 加英语本族施事词尾 -er。它的「编排活动」义产生于十九世纪；计算机义随电子机器在 1940 年代到来。年代均为约数。

items.en: The base noun descends from Greek programma, a written public notice, through Latin programma and French programme.
items.cn: 基础名词经拉丁语 programma 与法语 programme，源自希腊语 programma「公开书面通告」。

items.en: The ending -er is native English and marks the doer of an action; its use here is no different from writer or builder.
items.cn: 词尾 -er 是英语本族语素，标记动作的执行者；这里的用法与 writer、builder 并无不同。

items.en: A programmer first meant a person who arranged the programme of a concert or a ceremony, and the word is recorded in that sense before computing existed.
items.cn: programmer 最初指安排音乐会或仪式节目顺序的人，这一义在计算机出现之前已有记录。

items.en: In the 1940s the operators who prepared instruction sequences for electronic computers were called programmers, and the title spread with the industry.
items.cn: 1940 年代，为电子计算机准备指令序列的操作者被称为 programmer，这一头衔随产业扩散。

items.en: Later prefixes such as systems, applications and statistical split the one craft into named roles without changing the base meaning.
items.cn: 后来系统、应用、统计等前缀把这门手艺分成具名岗位，但基础含义未变。

items.en: The base noun plus the native agent ending is a transparent English formation recorded from the nineteenth century. Only the earliest dates of the two senses are approximate, and any deeper Indo-European root for graphein is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 首见年代不确定：基础名词加英语本族施事词尾，是构词清楚的英语形式，十九世纪已有书证；只是两个义项的最早年代为约数，为 graphein 提出的更早印欧语词根属于重构形式。

note.en: The first group is the same stem with other endings; the second group names neighbouring software roles and the older event planner.
note.cn: 第一组是同一词干加不同词尾；第二组是与软件岗位相邻的职业，以及较早的活动编排者。

entries.definition: The instructions themselves; a programmer produces a program, so the two differ as doer and product.
entries.definitionCN: 指指令本身；程序员产出程序，二者是「做的人」与「成品」的关系。

entries.definition: The work the programmer does; the person and the activity share one base and differ only in ending.
entries.definitionCN: 指程序员所做的工作；人与活动共享一个词基，只差词尾。

entries.definition: The British spelling of the product noun, especially the printed order of a performance.
entries.definitionCN: 成品名词的英式拼写，尤指演出的印刷节目单。

entries.definition: Able to take a new sequence; it describes the equipment a programmer works on, not the person.
entries.definitionCN: 指能装入新序列；它描述程序员操作的设备，而不是人。

entries.definition: A broader software role that also covers design, requirements and release work; a programmer may be one part of that role.
entries.definitionCN: 更宽的软件岗位，还涵盖设计、需求与发布；程序员可能只是其中一部分。

entries.definition: An informal word for someone who writes code, often implying craft without design responsibility.
entries.definitionCN: 写代码者的口语说法，常暗示只管实现、不管设计。

entries.definition: A title stressing systematic design and standards; software engineer is often the formal version of programmer.
entries.definitionCN: 强调系统设计与规范的职称；软件工程师常是程序员的正式说法。

entries.definition: The person who selects and arranges a programme of works or events; close to the older sense of programmer, but with an emphasis on care and selection.
entries.definitionCN: 挑选并安排作品或活动顺序的人；接近 programmer 的较早词义，但更强调挑选与照管。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real base noun, the real agent ending and the real job titles, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的基础名词、真实的施事词尾与真实职位名，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Program plus -er: the ending marks the person, so programmer is the one who writes the program.
normal.cn: program 加 -er：词尾标记人，所以 programmer 就是写程序的人。

normal.en: The family runs programmer, programming, program, programmable and reprogram.
normal.cn: 同族词有 programmer、programming、program、programmable 与 reprogram。

normal.en: Job titles mark the specialities: systems programmer, application programmer, statistical programmer.
normal.cn: 职位名标出专长：系统程序员、应用开发程序员、统计程序员。

normal.en: The older sense survives in arts administration, where a festival programmer arranges the season.
normal.cn: 较早的词义仍在艺术管理里存活：音乐节的节目编排者安排整个演出季。

normal.en: A programmer works on a program, and the two words differ only by the ending -er.
normal.cn: 程序员做的是程序，两个词只差词尾 -er。

abstract.en: Picture a person who reads a wall of errors the way a doctor reads a rash.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人读满屏报错，像医生看一片疹子。

abstract.en: Picture a hand that stops mid-key because the next line would change everything.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手停在按键上方，因为下一行会改变一切。

abstract.en: Picture a playbill being rearranged by someone who will never meet the performers.
abstract.cn: 想象有人反复调整节目单，却永远不会见到台上的演员。

examples.en: A programmer often spends more time reading code than writing it.
examples.cn: 程序员读代码的时间往往比写代码多。

examples.en: The festival programmer placed the new work after the symphony.
examples.cn: 音乐节编排者把新作排在了交响曲之后。

examples.en: The statistical programmer checked every table before the report was filed.
examples.cn: 统计程序员在报告提交前核对了每张表。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑（pro）来（gram）马（mer）」——扑到键盘前写程序的那匹马，就是程序员

root: 希腊 programma「公开书面通告」→ 拉丁 programma → 法语 programme → 英语 program；加英语施事词尾 -er 构成 programmer。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses divide into two lives of one word: the computing craft with its specialities, and the older role of arranging an event or a broadcast.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项分属这个词的两段生涯：计算机手艺及其细分岗位，以及较早的编排活动与播出内容的角色。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person at a keyboard, reading a wall of errors and writing the line that fixes them.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人在键盘前读满屏报错，写下能修好它的那一行。

branches.en: CRAFT AND JOB: the person who writes code, and the same craft turned into a paid team role.
branches.cn: 手艺与职业：写代码的人，以及同一门手艺变成的受雇团队岗位。

branches.en: DEPTH: systems programming marks how close the work sits to the machine.
branches.cn: 深度：系统编程标出工作离机器有多近。

branches.en: DOMAIN: industrial control and statistics both add an adjective instead of inventing a new noun.
branches.cn: 领域：工业控制与统计都只加一个形容词，而不另造名词。

branches.en: EVENT ORDER: festivals and channels are programmed by people, long before code existed.
branches.cn: 活动顺序：音乐节与频道由人编排，远在代码出现之前。

branches.en: DEVICE SETTING: loading a small sequence into a household unit is the domestic echo of the craft.
branches.cn: 设备设定：往家用设备里装入小序列，是这门手艺在家庭里的回声。

intro.en: Programmer is a Greek-derived base wearing the native English agent ending -er, the same pattern as writer and builder.
intro.cn: programmer 是希腊来源的词基戴着英语本族施事词尾 -er，与 writer、builder 同一模式。

latinIntro.en: Latin contributes the noun programma, which carried the word into French; the agent ending itself is English, not Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语贡献了名词 programma，把词带到法语；施事词尾本身是英语的，不是拉丁语。

items.example: The base carries the image of something written down.
items.exampleCN: 词基带着「写下来的东西」这一意象。

items.meaning: a plan; a set of instructions
items.example: The base noun supplies both the planning and computing senses.
items.exampleCN: 基础名词同时提供「计划」与「计算机」两个词义。

items.example: The ending is the only difference from the activity noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾是与「活动名词」的唯一差别。

items.example: The title is recorded before electronic computers existed.
items.exampleCN: 这个头衔在电子计算机出现之前已有记录。

items.example: The activity and the person share one base.
items.exampleCN: 活动与人共享一个词基。

items.structure: systems (English noun used as a prefix)
items.meaning: the whole machine and its software layers
items.example: Systems programmer marks work near the operating system.
items.exampleCN: 系统程序员标出靠近操作系统的工作。

items.meaning: relating to the analysis of data
items.example: Statistical programmer is a fixed role in clinical research.
items.exampleCN: 统计编程人员是临床研究里的固定岗位。

items.example: The programmer may reprogram the device.
items.exampleCN: 程序员可以重新给设备编程。

items.example: Programmable hardware takes new code from the programmer.
items.exampleCN: 可编程硬件接收程序员的新代码。

definition_zh: 对流；靠流体流动传递热量；对流环流
definition_en: the transfer of heat by the movement of a fluid such as air or water
core_image: 锅底受热的水向上涌起，表面的冷水下沉，形成一圈不断滚动的环流
scene: 厨房里，热空气在烤箱内被风扇推着循环，厨师说 In a convection oven, moving air carries heat to every shelf.
sceneCN: 这里 convection 指「靠流体流动把热从一个地方带到另一个地方」（第 4 个义项：烤箱内用风扇制造强制对流，使各层受热均匀）；句意为在对流烤箱里，流动的空气把热送到每一层架子。图中可辨识物件：烤箱、风扇、热气流箭头、烤盘。

derivatives.zh: 对流的；与对流有关的
使对流；靠对流传递
对流性的（如对流雨）
被对流带动的

senses.title: Heat carried by a moving fluid
senses.titleCN: 流体流动带走热量的传热方式
senses.definition: heat transfer in which the heated fluid itself moves and carries thermal energy with it
senses.definitionCN: 受热的流体本身发生移动，并把热能一起带走的传热方式
senses.example: Water at the bottom of the pot warms and rises by convection.
senses.exampleCN: 锅底的水受热后靠对流上升。
senses.why: Latin convehere means 'to carry together', so convection is literally heat being carried along by a moving medium.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 convehere 意为「一起搬运」，因此对流字面上就是热被流动的介质带着走。

senses.title: Rising air in the atmosphere
senses.definition: the vertical movement of warm, moist air that rises and cools, often forming clouds
senses.definitionCN: 暖湿空气上升并冷却的垂直运动，常形成云
senses.example: Afternoon convection built a tall column of cloud over the hills.
senses.exampleCN: 午后的对流在山丘上空堆起一根高高的云柱。
senses.why: The atmosphere is a fluid, so the same physical process is watched on a weather-chart scale.
senses.whyCN: 大气也是流体，因此同一物理过程被放在天气图的尺度上观察。

senses.title: Slow flow inside the Earth
senses.definition: the very slow circulation of hot rock in the mantle that helps drive plate motion
senses.definitionCN: 地幔中炽热岩石的极缓慢环流，它推动板块运动
senses.example: Mantle convection is too slow to see but strong enough to move continents.
senses.exampleCN: 地幔对流慢到看不见，却强到足以移动大陆。
senses.why: The medium here is solid rock behaving like an extremely viscous fluid over geological time.
senses.whyCN: 这里的介质是岩石，只是在漫长的地质时间里表现得像极黏稠的流体。

senses.title: Forced convection in appliances
senses.definition: convection driven by a fan or pump rather than by temperature differences alone
senses.definitionCN: 由风扇或泵而非单纯温差驱动的对流
senses.example: The convection oven finishes the roast in less time than a still oven.
senses.exampleCN: 对流烤箱比普通静置烤箱更快把肉烤好。
senses.why: Adding a fan turns a natural tendency into an engineered process, but the name of the process stays the same.
senses.whyCN: 加一个风扇把自然趋势变成工程过程，但过程的名称不变。

senses.title: A circulating loop of fluid
senses.definition: a closed loop in which warm fluid rises at one place and cool fluid sinks at another
senses.definitionCN: 暖流体在一处上升、冷流体在另一处下沉所形成的闭合环路
senses.example: A convection current in the room kept the smoke moving toward the door.
senses.exampleCN: 房间里的对流环流让烟一直朝门口飘。
senses.why: The loop is the visible shape the process takes, so the same word names the circulation and its cause.
senses.whyCN: 这个环路是过程呈现出的可见形状，因此同一个词既指环流也指其成因。

senses.title: Rain produced by rising air
senses.definition: heavy rain that falls when warm air rises quickly, cools and condenses in a tall cloud
senses.definitionCN: 暖空气迅速上升、冷却并在高云中凝结后落下的大雨
senses.example: Convection brought a short, violent storm just after noon.
senses.exampleCN: 对流在刚过正午时带来一场短促的暴雨。
senses.why: Meteorology names the rainfall after its cause, so convection stands for the whole convective weather event.
senses.whyCN: 气象学以成因给降雨命名，因此 convection 也代表整个对流性天气事件。

senses.title: Figurative spread of feeling or ideas
senses.titleCN: 比喻义：情绪或思想的涌动传播
senses.definition: the spreading of excitement, anger or ideas through a group as if carried by a rising current
senses.definitionCN: 兴奋、愤怒或思想像被上升气流带着一样在群体中扩散
senses.example: A convection of rumour moved through the office before lunch.
senses.exampleCN: 午饭前，一股谣言的暗流在办公室里涌动。
senses.why: The metaphor keeps the physics: something hot rises and carries other things with it.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻保留了物理内核：热的东西上升，并带走别的东西。

senses.title: The convective layer of a star
senses.definition: the outer region of a star where energy is carried outward by rising and sinking gas
senses.definitionCN: 恒星外部由气体升降把能量向外输送的区域
senses.example: The Sun's convection zone churns plasma beneath the visible surface.
senses.exampleCN: 太阳的对流层在可见表面之下翻搅着等离子体。
senses.why: Astrophysics applies the terrestrial fluid process to gas on a stellar scale.
senses.whyCN: 天体物理学把地球上的流体过程套用到恒星尺度的气体上。

intro.en: Convection comes from Latin convehere 'to carry together', built on com- 'together' and vehere 'to carry'. The noun convectio existed in Latin, and English first used the word for conveying before it became a term of physics.
intro.cn: convection 来自拉丁语 convehere「一起搬运」，由 com-「一起」与 vehere「搬运」构成。拉丁语本有名词 convectio；英语最初用它表示「传送」，后来才成为物理术语。

items.en: Vehere meant 'to carry, convey', with the past participle vectus; it is the source of vehicle and vector.
items.cn: vehere 意为「搬运、运送」，过去分词为 vectus；它是 vehicle 与 vector 的来源。

items.en: Com- 'together' plus vehere produced convehere 'to carry or bring together'.
items.cn: com-「一起」加 vehere 构成 convehere「一起搬运、聚集」。

items.en: The action noun convectio 'a bringing together, conveyance' supplied the shape of the English word.
items.cn: 动作名词 convectio「聚拢、运送」提供了英语词的形态。

items.en: English borrowed the word in the seventeenth century in the general sense of conveying; the physical sense developed later.
items.cn: 英语在 17 世纪借入这个词，泛指「传送」；物理义后来才发展出来。

items.en: The heat-transfer sense belongs to the nineteenth century, when heat was studied as a fluid-like quantity; the exact first use is uncertain.
items.cn: 传热义属于 19 世纪，当时热被当作类流体来研究；确切的最早使用不确定。

note.en: Group one holds words that resemble convection in form but come from other roots; group two holds the other modes of heat transfer and related circulation terms.
note.cn: 第一组是形式相近但词根不同的词；第二组是其他传热方式与相关的环流词。

entries.definition: From Latin convenire 'to come together', built on venire 'to come', not vehere 'to carry'; it means a custom or a meeting.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 convenire「聚到一起」，词根是 venire「来」而非 vehere「搬运」；意为惯例或会议。

entries.definition: From convertere 'to turn around', with the root vertere 'to turn'; it names a change of form or belief.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 convertere「转向」，词根为 vertere「转」；指形式或信仰的改变。

entries.definition: From convexus 'arched', with no carrying element at all; it describes a surface curving outward.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 convexus「拱起的」，完全没有「搬运」成分；形容向外凸起的表面。

entries.definition: Through Old French from Latin convehere: to carry something or to communicate an idea, but not the scientific process.
entries.definitionCN: 经古法语来自拉丁 convehere：搬运某物或传达想法，但不是科学过程。

entries.definition: Heat passing through a solid by direct contact between particles, with no bulk movement of the material.
entries.definitionCN: 热通过粒子间的直接接触穿过固体，物质本身不发生整体移动。

entries.definition: Heat travelling as electromagnetic waves, needing no medium at all.
entries.definitionCN: 热以电磁波形式传播，完全不需要介质。

entries.definition: The horizontal carrying of heat or moisture by wind; convection is mainly vertical, advection mainly horizontal.
entries.definitionCN: 风把热或水汽水平搬运；对流主要是垂直的，平流主要是水平的。

entries.definition: The movement of a fluid around a closed path; it is the shape convection takes, not the heat-transfer mechanism.
entries.definitionCN: 流体沿闭合路径的运动；它是对流呈现的形状，而非传热机制本身。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Latin morphemes, real compounds and real physics collocations, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁构词成分、真实复合词与真实物理搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: con- 'together' + vehere 'carry': the fluid carries heat along with it.
normal.cn: con-「一起」+ vehere「搬运」：流体把热一起带走。

normal.en: The same root appears in convey, vehicle and vector.
normal.cn: 同一词根出现在 convey、vehicle 与 vector 中。

normal.en: Physics pairs it with conduction and radiation as the three modes of heat transfer.
normal.cn: 物理学把它与 conduction、radiation 并列为三种传热方式。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the fields: convection oven, convection current, mantle convection.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：对流烤箱、对流环流、地幔对流。

normal.en: The adjective is convective and the verb is convect, both built on the same stem.
normal.cn: 形容词是 convective，动词是 convect，都基于同一词干。

abstract.en: Picture a pot of soup where the hot part climbs and the cool part dives, over and over.
abstract.cn: 想象一锅汤，热的部分往上爬，冷的部分往下沉，周而复始。

abstract.en: Picture a rumour rising in one office and drifting down into the next.
abstract.cn: 想象一则谣言在一间办公室升起，又飘进下一间。

abstract.en: Picture a slow stone river under the continents, moving a centimetre a year.
abstract.cn: 想象大陆之下一条缓慢的石河，一年只移动一厘米。

examples.en: Convection carries heat from the radiator to the far side of the room.
examples.cn: 对流把热从暖气片带到房间的另一头。

examples.en: The storm was fuelled by strong convection over warm water.
examples.cn: 暖水面上强烈的对流给这场风暴提供了能量。

examples.en: Geologists model mantle convection to explain continental drift.
examples.cn: 地质学家模拟地幔对流来解释大陆漂移。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一起背」——热和水汽一起被背着往上走，就是对流

root: 拉丁 convehere「一起搬运」= com-「一起」+ vehere「搬运、运送」，动作名词 convectio。英语 17 世纪借入时泛指「传送」，19 世纪才固定为传热术语；该物理义的最早书证不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one line: a moving fluid picks up heat and carries it away, whether in a pot, the sky, the mantle, an oven, a room, a storm, a crowd or a star.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一条线索展开：流动的流体带走热量，无论在锅里、天空、地幔、烤箱、房间、风暴、人群中还是恒星里。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: warm water rising at the bottom of a pot while cooler water sinks.
core.cn: 核心意象：锅底的热水上升，较冷的水下沉。

branches.en: PROCESS AND LOOP: the same word names the carrying and the circulating shape it makes.
branches.cn: 过程与环路：同一个词既指搬运，也指它形成的环流形状。

branches.en: WEATHER: rising air builds cloud and then releases rain.
branches.cn: 天气：上升的空气堆起云，随后落下雨。

branches.en: DEEP AND HIGH: the process works in mantle rock and in stellar gas.
branches.cn: 深处与高处：这一过程既发生在地幔岩石里，也发生在恒星气体里。

branches.en: ENGINEERED AIR: a fan turns natural convection into a controlled oven process.
branches.cn: 工程气流：风扇把自然对流变成可控的烤箱过程。

branches.en: SOCIAL CURRENT: excitement and rumour rise and spread like warm air.
branches.cn: 社会气流：兴奋与谣言像暖空气一样上升扩散。

intro.en: Convection is a Latin prefix, root and suffix laid end to end: con- plus vehere plus -tion. The same pieces build convey and convection's scientific relatives.
intro.cn: convection 是拉丁前缀、词根与后缀依次相接：con- 加 vehere 加 -tion。相同的成分还构成 convey 与对流的相关科学词。

latinIntro.en: Latin vehere gives a real family: vehere itself, the compound convehere, the action noun convectio, and the participle vectus.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 vehere 给出一个真实的词族：vehere 本身、复合词 convehere、动作名词 convectio 以及分词 vectus。

items.example: The prefix joins the carrying action to a group.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把搬运动作收拢到一个整体里。

items.example: The root underlies vehicle and vector.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根是 vehicle 与 vector 的基础。

items.meaning: the act or result of an action
items.example: The suffix turns convect into the name of a process.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把 convect 变成过程之名。

items.meaning: to move heat by fluid motion
items.example: The fan convects warm air through the room.
items.exampleCN: 风扇让暖空气在房间里对流。

items.example: Convective clouds grow tall in the afternoon.
items.exampleCN: 对流的云在午后长得高大。

items.example: The layer is convectively unstable.
items.exampleCN: 这一层在对流上是不稳定的。

items.meaning: produced by convection, as of rainfall
items.example: Convectional rain fell in the early afternoon.
items.exampleCN: 对流雨在午后早些时候落下。

items.example: The letter conveyed the news quietly.
items.exampleCN: 这封信平静地传达了消息。

definition_zh: 恒星星等；表示恒星亮度的对数标尺数值
definition_en: a number on a logarithmic scale that expresses how bright a star appears or how much light it truly emits
core_image: 夜空里一排星点旁标着由负到正的刻度，越亮的星数字越小
scene: 天文台圆顶里，观测者把同一片星场拍下来，逐颗比对亮度，写下每颗星的等级。 The chart lists the stellar magnitude of every star in the cluster.
sceneCN: 这里指「用对数标尺表示恒星亮度的数值」（第 1 个义项：视星等，数值越小表示越亮）；句意为星图列出这个星团中每颗恒星的星等。图中可辨识物件：星图、圆顶、望远镜、铅笔记录。

pos.zh: 恒星星等（可数，复数为 stellar magnitudes）

derivatives.zh: 恒星的；星形的
巨大；量值；星等
放大；夸大

senses.title: Apparent brightness rank of a star
senses.definition: the rank of a star's brightness as seen from Earth, with smaller numbers for brighter stars
senses.definitionCN: 从地球看到的恒星亮度等级，星越亮数值越小
senses.example: The chart lists the stellar magnitude of every star in the cluster.
senses.exampleCN: 星图列出这个星团中每颗恒星的星等。
senses.why: stellar supplies the object and magnitude supplies the ranked number, so the phrase reads as the brightness rank of a star.
senses.whyCN: stellar 提供对象，magnitude 提供等级数值，因此整个短语读作「恒星的亮度等级」。

senses.title: Absolute brightness rank
senses.definition: the brightness a star would have if placed at a standard distance of ten parsecs
senses.definitionCN: 把恒星放在十秒差距的标准距离上时它应有的亮度
senses.example: Absolute stellar magnitude removes distance from the comparison.
senses.exampleCN: 绝对星等把距离因素从比较中剔除。
senses.why: the adjective absolute marks a value freed from the observer's position, while the base term still means ranked brightness.
senses.whyCN: 形容词 absolute 标记一个脱离观测位置的值，而基本术语仍指分级的亮度。

senses.title: The logarithmic scale itself
senses.definition: the five-step logarithmic system in which a difference of five magnitudes equals a factor of one hundred in brightness
senses.definitionCN: 五级一档的对数体系，星等相差五级即亮度相差一百倍
senses.example: On the stellar magnitude scale, a difference of five means a hundredfold change.
senses.exampleCN: 在星等标尺上，相差五级意味着亮度变化一百倍。
senses.why: the phrase can name not just a reading but the ladder the reading sits on.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语不仅可以指一个读数，也可以指读数所在的那把梯子。

senses.title: Negative magnitude for very bright objects
senses.definition: a magnitude below zero, assigned to objects brighter than the zero point such as Venus or Sirius
senses.definitionCN: 低于零的星等，赋给比零点更亮的天体，如金星或天狼星
senses.example: Sirius carries a negative stellar magnitude in most modern catalogues.
senses.exampleCN: 在多数现代星表里，天狼星的星等为负。
senses.why: because the scale was built backwards, the brightest objects fall below zero and take negative numbers.
senses.whyCN: 由于标尺是倒着建立的，最亮的天体会落到零以下，取负值。

senses.title: Magnitude difference and flux ratio
senses.definition: the numerical gap between two magnitudes, from which the ratio of received light is calculated
senses.definitionCN: 两个星等之间的数值差，据此算出来光量的比值
senses.example: A stellar magnitude difference of one corresponds to about two and a half times the light.
senses.exampleCN: 星等相差一级，约对应两点五倍的光量。
senses.why: the scale is logarithmic, so subtraction on the magnitude side becomes division on the light side.
senses.whyCN: 标尺是对数的，因此在星等一侧做减法，相当于在光量一侧做除法。

senses.title: Photometric magnitude in a band
senses.definition: a magnitude measured through a specified filter or wavelength band
senses.definitionCN: 通过特定滤光片或波段测得的星等
senses.example: The survey reports a stellar magnitude in the red band for each source.
senses.exampleCN: 巡天为每个源给出红波段的星等。
senses.why: instruments do not see all wavelengths at once, so the phrase is qualified by the band being measured.
senses.whyCN: 仪器不能一次看见所有波长，因此这个短语要用所测波段来限定。

senses.title: A value kept in a star catalogue
senses.definition: a published magnitude recorded in a catalogue and reused by later observers
senses.definitionCN: 记录在星表中、供后来观测者沿用的星等
senses.example: The old stellar magnitude in the catalogue was half a step too bright.
senses.exampleCN: 星表里的旧星等偏亮了半级。
senses.why: catalogues preserve numbers across centuries, so the phrase also names a historical record.
senses.whyCN: 星表把数字保存数百年，因此这个短语也指一份历史记录。

senses.title: Figurative rank of importance
senses.definition: a borrowed use in which people or events are ranked like stars on the brightness scale
senses.definitionCN: 借用星等标尺给人或事件排出的重要等级
senses.example: In the world of violin making, he is of the first stellar magnitude.
senses.exampleCN: 在小提琴制作界，他属于第一等。
senses.why: the reversed scale became an idiom of rank, and the adjective stellar adds the sense of excellence.
senses.whyCN: 这套倒序标尺成了表示等级的说法，而形容词 stellar 又添上「卓越」之意。

intro.en: Stellar magnitude joins Latin stellaris 'of stars' to Latin magnitudo 'greatness'. The technical sense was fixed by astronomers in the nineteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: stellar magnitude 把拉丁 stellaris「星的」与拉丁 magnitudo「巨大」连接起来；这一技术义由十九世纪的天文学家固定。年代均为约数。

items.en: Stella 'star' produced stellaris 'of stars'. The deeper origin of stella is uncertain; the link to a reconstructed *ster- 'star' is a hypothesis shared with Greek aster.
items.cn: stella「星」构成 stellaris「星的」。stella 更深来源不确定；与重构词根 *ster-「星」的联系只是与希腊语 aster 共享的假说。

items.en: Magnitudo 'greatness, size' came from magnus 'great' plus -tudo, a state suffix.
items.cn: magnitudo「巨大、规模」来自 magnus「大的」加表状态的后缀 -tudo。

items.en: Greek and later Arabic star lists sorted stars into six brightness classes, the practice that gave magnitude its astronomical sense.
items.cn: 希腊与后来的阿拉伯星表把恒星分成六个亮度等级，这一做法赋予 magnitude 天文学含义。

items.en: Photometry made the old classes numerical and logarithmic, and the phrase stellar magnitude settled into its modern meaning.
items.cn: 测光学使旧的等级变成数值与对数关系，stellar magnitude 这一短语也固定为现代含义。

items.en: Twentieth-century surveys added band-specific magnitudes and absolute magnitudes, extending the phrase rather than replacing it.
items.cn: 二十世纪的巡天增添了分波段星等与绝对星等，扩展了这一短语而非取代它。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin only): both stella and magnus lack established Indo-European ancestors, so the roots often printed for them are reconstructions.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅更深词源）：stella 与 magnus 都没有已确定的印欧祖先，常为它们印出的词根均属重构。

note.en: Group one holds the magnitude labels that are routinely swapped; group two holds words for brightness and light output.
note.cn: 第一组是常被互换的星等标签；第二组是表示亮度与光输出的词。

entries.definition: The brightness actually seen from Earth, which includes the effect of distance; stellar magnitude alone does not say which value is meant.
entries.definitionCN: 从地球实际看到的亮度，包含距离影响；单说 stellar magnitude 并未指明是哪一种值。

entries.definition: The brightness a star would show at ten parsecs, used to compare true luminosity.
entries.definitionCN: 恒星在十秒差距处应有的亮度，用于比较真实光度。

entries.definition: A magnitude integrated over the whole spectrum, not through one band.
entries.definitionCN: 在整个光谱上积分的星等，而非通过某一波段测得。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning 'of stars'; it cannot stand alone for the number, which is the magnitude.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「恒星的」的形容词；它不能单独指那个数值，数值由 magnitude 承担。

entries.definition: The actual amount of light received; magnitude is the rank assigned on a logarithmic scale.
entries.definitionCN: 实际接收到的光量；magnitude 是在对数标尺上赋予的等级。

entries.definition: The total energy a star radiates per second, an intrinsic physical quantity rather than a rank.
entries.definitionCN: 恒星每秒辐射的总能量，是内禀物理量而非等级。

entries.definition: The energy arriving per unit area per unit time; it is the physical input from which a magnitude is calculated.
entries.definitionCN: 单位面积单位时间到达的能量；是由它算出星等的物理输入。

entries.definition: The light level as observed, without converting it into the magnitude scale.
entries.definitionCN: 观测到的光量水平，尚未换算成星等标尺。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real astronomical usage and real Latin pieces, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的天文用法与真实的拉丁成分，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Smaller number, brighter star: the scale runs backwards.
normal.cn: 数字越小，星越亮：这套标尺是倒着的。

normal.en: Five magnitudes equal a hundredfold change in brightness.
normal.cn: 五个星等等于亮度一百倍的变化。

normal.en: Apparent magnitude includes distance; absolute magnitude removes it.
normal.cn: 视星等包含距离；绝对星等排除距离。

normal.en: The phrase is stellar (of stars) plus magnitude (ranked size).
normal.cn: 这个短语是 stellar「星的」加 magnitude「分级大小」。

normal.en: Of the first magnitude survives as an idiom of rank.
normal.cn: 头等重要的说法作为表示等级的成语留存下来。

abstract.en: Picture a ladder where the top rung is labelled with the smallest number.
abstract.cn: 想象一架梯子，最上面那级标着最小的数字。

abstract.en: Picture two lamps, one near and one far, looking equally bright to your eye.
abstract.cn: 想象两盏灯，一近一远，在你眼里却一样亮。

abstract.en: Picture a night sky sorted into ranks by a patient ancient observer.
abstract.cn: 想象一位耐心的古代观测者把夜空分成等级。

examples.en: The telescope reaches stars of stellar magnitude fourteen.
examples.cn: 这台望远镜能观测到十四等的恒星。

examples.en: Astronomers converted the old stellar magnitude into a modern flux measurement.
examples.cn: 天文学家把旧星等换算成现代的光通量测量值。

examples.en: Her reputation in the field is of the first stellar magnitude.
examples.cn: 她在这一领域的声望属第一等。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「stellar（恒星的）+ magnitude（等级数值）」——给恒星亮度排出的等级 → 星等

root: 拉丁 stellaris「星的」来自 stella「星」，其更深来源不确定；拉丁 magnitudo「巨大」来自 magnus「大的」加 -tudo（状态）。stella 与 magnus 的印欧词根均属重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one number: it ranks a star as seen, as it truly is, as a scale, below zero, as a difference, through a filter, as a catalogue entry and finally as a human rank.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一个数值：它给恒星排出视亮度、真实亮度、标尺本身、零下取值、差值、波段读数、星表记录，最后是人的等级。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a night sky graded by a reversed ruler, the brightest star carrying the smallest mark.
core.cn: 核心意象：夜空被一把倒置的尺子分级，最亮的星带着最小的刻度。

branches.en: A RANK AND A LADDER: one reading and the system that produces it.
branches.cn: 等级与梯子：一个读数，以及产生它的体系。

branches.en: DISTANCE REMOVED: the same rank recalculated at a standard distance.
branches.cn: 去掉距离：同一等级在标准距离上重算。

branches.en: BELOW ZERO AND ON PAPER: bright objects go negative, and catalogues keep the number.
branches.cn: 零下与纸上：极亮天体取负值，星表把数字留存。

branches.en: DIFFERENCE AND BAND: subtraction on the scale, measurement through a filter.
branches.cn: 差值与波段：标尺上做减法，滤光片里做测量。

branches.en: HUMAN RANK: the star scale becomes a way of grading people.
branches.cn: 人的等级：星等标尺变成给人分级的方式。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Latin adjective of stars to a Latin noun of greatness, so both halves carry recognisable relatives.
intro.cn: 这个短语把表示「星的」拉丁形容词与表示「巨大」的拉丁名词连接起来，两半都有可辨认的同族词。

latinIntro.en: Stella and stellaris supply the first half; magnus, magnitudo and -tudo supply the second.
latinIntro.cn: stella 与 stellaris 提供前半；magnus、magnitudo 与 -tudo 提供后半。

items.example: Stella is the root of stellar and interstellar.
items.exampleCN: stella 是 stellar 与 interstellar 的词根。

items.example: Stellaris gives the English stellar.
items.exampleCN: stellaris 构成英语 stellar。

items.example: Stellar light takes years to reach us.
items.exampleCN: 星光要多年才到达我们。

items.example: Magnus is the root of magnitude.
items.exampleCN: magnus 是 magnitude 的词根。

items.example: The suffix builds nouns of state.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成表状态的名词。

items.example: The magnitude of the star was recorded.
items.exampleCN: 这颗星的星等被记录下来。

items.example: Dust clouds fill interstellar space.
items.exampleCN: 尘埃云充满星际空间。

items.example: The lens magnifies the star's image.
items.exampleCN: 镜片放大恒星的像。

items.example: The poem describes a stelliferous sky.
items.exampleCN: 这首诗描写布满星辰的夜空。

items.example: The magnitude scale runs in reverse.
items.exampleCN: 星等标尺是倒序的。

latinEntries.structure: magnus, magna, magnum (adj., first and second declension)

definition_zh: 凉亭；藤架；（古）乔木；树
definition_en: a leafy shelter formed by trees or climbing plants on a frame; formerly, a tree
core_image: 藤蔓爬满木架：绿色的屋顶下藏着一张长凳
scene: 花园深处，葡萄藤在头顶交缠，阳光漏下点点碎金。 The couple sat reading beneath the rose arbor.
sceneCN: 这里 arbor 是「藤架、凉亭」（第 1 个义项：植物搭成的荫棚）；句意为：这对伴侣坐在玫瑰花架下读书。

derivatives.zh: 同根形容词，义为「树的；栖于树的」
同根名词，义为「植物园；树木园」
复合称谓，义为「树木园管理员」
同根派生，义为「树艺师」

senses.title: A shelter of climbing plants
senses.definition: a frame over which vines or roses are trained to make a leafy shelter
senses.definitionCN: 藤蔓或蔷薇攀爬其上形成绿荫的架子
senses.example: Wisteria covered the garden arbor.
senses.exampleCN: 紫藤爬满了园中的藤架。
senses.why: The root means tree; a leafy shelter is a small made tree.
senses.whyCN: 词根本义是树；绿荫棚就是一座人造小树。

senses.title: A garden retreat
senses.definition: a shady nook in a garden for sitting and resting
senses.definitionCN: 园中供人落座休息的荫凉角落
senses.example: Grandmother shelled peas in the arbor.
senses.exampleCN: 祖母坐在凉亭里剥豌豆。
senses.why: Once the shelter exists, the place itself takes the name.
senses.whyCN: 荫棚一旦落成，其所在之处便承袭其名。

senses.title: A tree itself (archaic)
senses.definition: in older botanical and poetic use, a tree
senses.definitionCN: 旧时植物学与诗歌用语中指树木
senses.example: Old herbals divided plants into arbor, frutex, and herba.
senses.exampleCN: 古老的本草书把植物分为乔木、灌木与草本。
senses.why: This is the root meaning, kept in learned Latin labels.
senses.whyCN: 这是词根本义，保存在学术性的拉丁语标签中。

senses.title: The axis of a wheel or machine
senses.definition: the central shaft or spindle on which something turns
senses.definitionCN: 供部件旋转的中心轴或主轴
senses.example: The saw blade mounts on the arbor.
senses.exampleCN: 锯片安装在主轴上。
senses.why: A different Latin arbor (a shaft) blended with the tree word.
senses.whyCN: 另一个拉丁词 arbor（轴）与「树」一词混融。

senses.title: Anatomy: the arbor vitae
senses.definition: a branching structure resembling a tree, as in the cerebellum
senses.definitionCN: 形似树枝的分叉结构，如小脑中的生命之树
senses.example: The slice revealed the arbor vitae of the cerebellum.
senses.exampleCN: 切片显露出小脑的生命之树结构。
senses.why: Bodies grow trees too, so anatomy borrowed the image.
senses.whyCN: 身体里也长树，解剖学便借用了这一意象。

senses.title: A ceremonial or symbolic tree
senses.definition: a tree or tree-shaped structure used in festivals or as a symbol
senses.definitionCN: 节庆中使用的树或树形构筑物，作为象征
senses.example: Villagers raised a may arbor for the spring fair.
senses.exampleCN: 村民为春季集市竖起了五月花柱凉棚。
senses.why: Trees carry meanings: shelter, life, and gathering.
senses.whyCN: 树承载意义：庇护、生命与相聚。

senses.title: A family name of places
senses.definition: used in place names, most famously Ann Arbor
senses.definitionCN: 用于地名，最著名的是安阿伯（Ann Arbor）
senses.example: They moved to Ann Arbor for graduate school.

intro.en: Arbor is Latin for tree, and its English garden sense grew by way of Old French herbier and erber, a plot of green.
intro.cn: arbor 是拉丁语「树」，英语的园艺义经古法语 herbier/erber（绿地）演变而来。

items.en: The reconstructed root *h3erb- denoted plants or produce, source of Latin arbor.
items.cn: 重构词根 *h3erb- 指植物、出产，是拉丁语 arbor 的来源。

items.en: Arbor meant a tree, distinguished from shrubs and herbs.
items.cn: arbor 意为乔木，区别于灌木与草本。

items.en: Erber, from Latin herba, meant a grassy plot; herbier a green shelter.
items.cn: erber（源自拉丁语 herba）指草地；herbier 指绿色荫棚。

items.en: English blended arbor with erber, fixing the garden-shelter sense.
items.cn: 英语把 arbor 与 erber 融合，固定了「园中荫棚」之义。

items.en: Arbor now names garden shelters, with the tree sense alive in arboretum and arborist.
items.cn: 如今 arbor 指园中凉棚，树义则活在 arboretum、arborist 中。

note.en: Arbor heads a family of tree words and is often confused with harbor.
note.cn: arbor 是一族树词之首，且常与 harbor 混淆。

normalIntro.en: The tree-root family makes arbor and all its cousins easy.
normalIntro.cn: 「树」词根一族让 arbor 及其亲戚们全都好记。

normal.en: arbor is Latin for tree; the shelter is a little man-made tree.
normal.cn: arbor 是拉丁语「树」；荫棚就是人造的小树。

normal.en: Same family: arboreal (tree-dwelling), arboretum (tree garden), arborist (tree doctor).
normal.cn: 同族：arboreal（树栖的）、arboretum（树木园）、arborist（树艺师）。

normal.en: Arbor Day is the tree-planting holiday.
normal.cn: 植树节的英文名就是 Arbor Day。

normal.en: Contrast: arbor shelters plants; harbor shelters ships.
normal.cn: 对照：arbor 庇护植物，harbor 庇护船只。

normal.en: Place name: Ann Arbor keeps the old word alive.
normal.cn: 地名：Ann Arbor 让这个古词留存至今。

abstract.en: A green roof growing on wooden bones, cool shade underneath.
abstract.cn: 绿色屋顶长在木骨之上，底下是一片阴凉。

abstract.en: A giant leafy umbrella you can sit inside.
abstract.cn: 一把可以坐进去的巨大绿叶伞。

abstract.en: Arbor sounds like 'harbor' — the harbor of the garden, sheltering vines.
abstract.cn: arbor 听着像 harbor——花园的港湾，庇护着藤蔓。

examples.en: Grapes ripened over the old arbor.
examples.cn: 葡萄在老藤架上渐渐成熟。

examples.en: They built an arbor at the end of the garden path.
examples.cn: 他们在花园小径尽头搭了一座藤架。

examples.en: Birds nested in the arbor all summer.
examples.cn: 整个夏天，鸟儿都在凉棚里筑巢。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿婆」——阿婆最爱坐在藤架下乘凉，arbor 就是阿婆的凉棚，谐音仅助记。

definition_zh: 批评；非难；谴责性评论
definition_en: criticism or critical remark, especially a hostile or censorious comment
core_image: 目光转向、盯住过错：把心思转向别人的错处并说出口
scene: 评审会上，教授放下钢笔，皱起了眉。 The committee's report contained a sharp animadversion on the mayor's spending.
sceneCN: 这里 animadversion 是「批评、非难」（第 1 个义项：指责性的评论）；句意为：委员会的报告对市长的开支提出了尖锐的批评。

derivatives.zh: animadversion 的动词形式，义为「批评；指责」
罕见派生，义为「批评性的；非难的」

senses.title: A critical or censorious remark
senses.definition: a comment that points out fault or expresses disapproval
senses.definitionCN: 指出过错或表达不满的评论
senses.example: The essay opened with an animadversion on modern architecture.
senses.exampleCN: 文章以对现代建筑的批评开篇。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to turn the mind toward something, here toward its faults.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词本义是「把心神转向某物」，此处转向的是其过错。

senses.title: Hostile criticism of a person
senses.definition: disapproving comment directed at a person or their conduct
senses.definitionCN: 针对某人或其行为的不满评论
senses.example: His animadversions on the general were repeated all over town.
senses.exampleCN: 他对将军的责难传遍了全城。
senses.why: Turning the mind toward a person often means fixing the gaze on their flaws.
senses.whyCN: 把心神转向一个人，往往意味着紧盯其缺点。

senses.title: Official or formal censure
senses.definition: formal expression of disapproval by an authority
senses.definitionCN: 权威机构正式表达的不满
senses.example: The senate's animadversions forced the official to resign.
senses.exampleCN: 元老院的谴责迫使该官员辞职。
senses.why: When institutions turn their attention to a fault, the result is censure.
senses.whyCN: 当机构将注意力转向过错，结果便是正式申斥。

senses.title: Notice or observation preceding judgment
senses.definition: observation or comment, not necessarily unfavorable (older sense)
senses.definitionCN: 观察或评论，未必含贬义（旧义）
senses.example: Early uses allowed animadversion to mean simple notice of a thing.
senses.exampleCN: 早期用法中 animadversion 可仅指对某事的注意。
senses.why: Before the hostile sense hardened, turning the mind toward a thing was neutral attention.
senses.whyCN: 在贬义固化之前，「把心神转向某物」只是中性的关注。

senses.title: Criticism in writing or print
senses.definition: written critical remarks, as in reviews or polemics
senses.definitionCN: 书面的批评言论，如评论或论战文字
senses.example: The pamphlet collected animadversions against the new tax law.
senses.exampleCN: 这本小册子汇集了针对新税法的批评。
senses.why: Critical remarks fixed in print multiply and travel, extending the word's reach.
senses.whyCN: 批评言论一经印行便传播开来，扩展了该词的使用范围。

senses.title: Judicial animadversion: a judge's rebuke
senses.definition: a rebuke delivered by a court or judge from the bench
senses.definitionCN: 法庭或法官当庭发出的训斥
senses.example: The judge's animadversion warned the lawyer against delay tactics.
senses.exampleCN: 法官的训诫警告该律师不得拖延。
senses.why: The bench turns its official gaze on misconduct and speaks it aloud.
senses.whyCN: 法庭将官方目光投向不当行为并公开说出，即为司法训诫。

senses.title: Criticism of ideas or works rather than persons
senses.definition: critical evaluation aimed at theories, texts, or works
senses.definitionCN: 针对理论、文本或作品的批评性评价
senses.example: Scholarly animadversion refined the theory over decades.
senses.exampleCN: 学界的批评使这一理论在数十年间不断完善。
senses.why: The turned gaze can rest on books as well as deeds.
senses.whyCN: 这「转过去的目光」既可落在行为上，也可落在书卷上。

senses.title: Animadversion to or upon: the act of animadverting
senses.definition: the action of animadverting, taking notice with disapproval
senses.definitionCN: 进行批评、以不满态度加以指摘的行为
senses.example: His constant animadversion upon trivial matters wearied his friends.
senses.exampleCN: 他不断对琐事加以指摘，令朋友们厌倦。
senses.why: Repeating the turned gaze turns criticism into a habit, and the noun names the habit itself.
senses.whyCN: 反复「转动的目光」使批评成为习惯，名词即指这种习惯性行为。

intro.en: Animadversion literally means a turning of the mind toward something; in English it settled into meaning the remarks made when that something is a fault.
intro.cn: animadversion 字面是「心神转向某物」；在英语中定型为当所转向者是过错时发出的评论，即批评。

items.en: The roots *h₂enh₁- (to breathe) underlie Latin animus, the mind or spirit.
items.cn: 一般认为印欧词根 *h₂enh₁-（呼吸）是拉丁语 animus（心神、精神）的来源。

items.en: Animadvertere joined animus (mind) and advertere (to turn toward), meaning to turn the mind to a thing, notice it, then censure it.
items.cn: 拉丁语 animadvertere 由 animus（心神）与 advertere（转向）构成，义为「将心神转向、注意到，进而责备」。

items.en: The noun animadversio named the noticing and the censure that followed.
items.cn: 拉丁语名词 animadversio 指这种注意及随之而来的责备。

items.en: English took both verb and noun around 1600; at first the noun could mean simple observation.
items.cn: 英语约在 1600 年前后同时借入动词与名词；名词起初可仅指「注意、观察」。

items.en: The censorious sense prevailed, fixing animadversion as formal, often hostile criticism.
items.cn: 责难义逐渐占据主导，使 animadversion 定型为正式且常带敌意的批评。

normal.cn: animation 保留 animus 的「生气」义；animadversion 则把心神转向过错。

normal.en: Formal writing prefers animadversion to casual criticism.
normal.cn: 正式文体更常用 animadversion 而非随口的 criticism。

abstract.en: Picture a head turning sharply toward one small error on a long page.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗头颅猛然转向长卷上的一处小错。

abstract.en: See an arrow of attention piercing one flaw in an otherwise fine report.
abstract.cn: 想象一支「注意力之箭」射中报告中唯一的瑕疵。

abstract.en: Feel the room go quiet when the censor's gaze lands.
abstract.cn: 感受审视的目光落下时全场骤然的安静。

examples.en: The review was full of animadversions on the director's earlier films.
examples.cn: 这篇评论满是对导演早期作品的批评。

examples.en: She escaped animadversion because her report was flawless.
examples.cn: 由于报告无懈可击，她免于受到批评。

examples.en: His animadversion upon the policy was quoted for weeks.
