senses.title: Supply water to land or crops
senses.definition: to supply water to land, fields or growing plants, especially by artificial means
senses.definitionCN: 尤以人工方式向土地、田地或生长中的作物供水
senses.example: They irrigate the orchard every second week in summer.
senses.exampleCN: 夏天他们每隔一周给果园浇水。
senses.why: the core verb sense simply names the act that the noun irrigation also names.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词的核心义项就是名词 irrigation 所指的那个行为本身。

senses.title: Lead water through channels
senses.definition: to bring water to a field along ditches, pipes or furrows rather than by rainfall
senses.definitionCN: 沿沟渠、管道或垄沟把水送到田里，而非依赖降雨
senses.example: The farmers irrigate the lower plots from a single earthen canal.
senses.exampleCN: 农民们用一条土渠给低处的地块引水。
senses.why: the verb keeps the image of leading water along a path, which is the oldest technique.
senses.whyCN: 动词保留了「沿路径把水引过去」的意象，这是最古老的技术。

senses.title: Flush a wound
senses.definition: to wash a wound with a stream of water or saline so that debris is carried away
senses.definitionCN: 用水流或生理盐水冲洗伤口，把杂物带走
senses.example: The doctor irrigated the cut before closing it.
senses.exampleCN: 医生在缝合前冲洗了那道伤口。
senses.why: medicine extended the watering verb to the cleaning of tissue, since both involve a directed stream.
senses.whyCN: 医学把浇水这个动词扩展到清洁组织，因为二者都涉及定向的液流。

senses.title: Flush a body cavity
senses.definition: to flush a sinus, bladder or other cavity with liquid for treatment
senses.definitionCN: 为治疗目的用液体冲洗窦腔、膀胱或其他腔体
senses.example: The nurse irrigated the patient's ear to remove the blockage.
senses.exampleCN: 护士冲洗病人的耳朵以清除堵塞。
senses.why: the same stream that waters a field can clear a hollow space, so the verb spreads to cavities.
senses.whyCN: 浇田的那股水流也能清理一个空腔，动词便延伸到体腔。

senses.title: Of a river: to water
senses.definition: of a river or flood, to supply water to the land beside it
senses.definitionCN: 指河流或洪水给沿岸土地供水
senses.example: The river irrigates the plain each spring without any pump.
senses.exampleCN: 这条河每年春天不用任何水泵就浸润平原。
senses.why: water does the work by itself here, so the verb drops the idea of an engineer.
senses.whyCN: 这里水自己完成了工作，动词因此不再含「有工程师介入」的意思。

senses.title: Make dry land productive
senses.definition: to bring water to dry ground so that it can support crops
senses.definitionCN: 把水引到干旱的土地，使其能够种植作物
senses.example: The project irrigated the desert and doubled the harvest.
senses.exampleCN: 这个工程灌溉了荒漠，使收成翻倍。
senses.why: the purpose behind the act is to change what the land can do, and the verb can name that result.
senses.whyCN: 行为背后的目的是改变土地能做什么，动词因此可以指这一结果。

senses.title: Moisten something
senses.definition: to make something slightly wet, even where no crop is involved
senses.definitionCN: 使某物略微湿润，即使与作物无关
senses.example: Rain irrigated the dusty road and quieted the air.
senses.exampleCN: 雨水润湿了尘土飞扬的路，空气也静了下来。
senses.why: the Latin verb simply meant to moisten, and that broad sense survives beside the farming one.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词本义就是润湿，这个宽泛义项一直与农业义并存。

senses.title: Water turf and landscape
senses.definition: to keep lawns, parks or sports turf supplied with water by a built system
senses.definitionCN: 用建成系统为草坪、公园或运动场地持续供水
senses.example: Groundskeepers irrigate the pitch through buried sprinklers.
senses.exampleCN: 场地管理员通过埋设的喷头给球场浇水。
senses.why: the same act now serves appearance rather than harvest, and the verb follows it into that setting.
senses.whyCN: 同一行为如今服务于外观而非收成，动词也随之进入这一场景。

intro.en: Irrigate comes from Latin irrigare 'to water', from in- 'into' and rigare 'to moisten'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: irrigate 来自拉丁 irrigare「浇水」，由 in-「进入」与 rigare「润湿」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Rigare meant 'to water, moisten'. Its deeper origin is not established; the connections proposed with other watering verbs are hypotheses, so any earlier root offered for it is a reconstructed form.
items.cn: rigare 意为「浇水、润湿」。其更早来源尚无定论；有人提出的与别的「浇水」动词之间的联系都只是假说，因此为它给出的更早词根均属重构形式。

items.en: In- 'into' plus rigare produced irrigare 'to lead water into something'. The prefix assimilates to ir- before r, giving the spelling ir-.
items.cn: in-「进入」加 rigare 构成 irrigare「把水引入某物」，前缀在 r 前同化为 ir-，拼写遂作 ir-。

items.en: The past participle irrigatus 'watered' was used adjectivally of land and later of washed tissue.
items.cn: 过去分词 irrigatus「已浇过水的」先用于土地，后也用于被冲洗的组织。

items.en: Medical Latin applied the verb to the flushing of wounds and cavities with fluid, a use that English inherited.
items.cn: 医学拉丁语把这个动词用于以液体冲洗伤口与体腔，英语继承了这一用法。

items.en: English took the verb in the seventeenth century, first for watering land and soon after for washing body parts.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪引入这个动词，先指给土地浇水，随后又指冲洗身体部位。

items.en: Source uncertain: the pre-Latin origin of rigare is unsettled, and the first English date is not precisely recorded, so earlier forms given for the root are reconstructed rather than attested.
items.cn: 来源不确定：rigare 在拉丁语之前的来源无定论，英语首见的年代也没有精确记录，因此为这个词根给出的更早形式属重构形式而非书证。

note.en: Group one separates the verb from its own family and from the look-alike irritate, which shares sound but not origin; group two separates it from neighbouring water verbs.
note.cn: 第一组把这个动词与自己的词族以及形近而不同源的 irritate 分开；第二组把它与相邻的「水」类动词分开。

entries.definition: The action noun built on the verb; it names the act, the works or the water.
entries.definitionCN: 由动词构成的动作名词；指行为、工程或水。

entries.definition: Describes land that has received water; it is a state, not an action.
entries.definitionCN: 描述已受水的土地；是状态，不是动作。

entries.definition: From irritare 'to provoke'; it sounds close but carries no water at all.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 irritare「激怒」；读音接近，却完全不含水。

entries.definition: Says land can be watered; it does not describe anyone watering it.
entries.definitionCN: 指土地可以受水；并不描述有人在浇。

entries.definition: The everyday verb for giving plants water; irrigate implies method and scale.
entries.definitionCN: 给植物供水的日常动词；irrigate 含方法与规模之意。

entries.definition: To scatter drops over a surface; one way to irrigate, not the whole act.
entries.definitionCN: 把水滴散在表面；是灌溉的一种方式，而非整个行为。

entries.definition: To cover land with water deliberately; a technique, often a crude one.
entries.definitionCN: 有意让水覆盖土地；是一种技术，往往较粗放。

entries.definition: To clean with liquid; it covers the medical sense but not the farming one.
entries.definitionCN: 用液体清洁；覆盖医学义，却不覆盖农业义。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Latin verb, its real derivatives and the phrases in which it actually occurs.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：拉丁动词、其真实派生词，以及它实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Latin in- 'into' plus rigare 'to water': to lead water into the ground.
normal.cn: 拉丁 in-「进入」加 rigare「浇水」：把水引进地里。

normal.en: The family runs irrigate, irrigation, irrigator, irrigable, irrigational.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 irrigate、irrigation、irrigator、irrigable、irrigational。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the everyday uses: irrigate the fields, irrigate crops, irrigate a wound.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出日常用法：灌溉田地、浇灌作物、冲洗伤口。

normal.en: The medical use keeps the same image: a stream is aimed at one spot and carries dirt away.
normal.cn: 医学用法保留同一意象：一股液流对准一处，把脏物带走。

normal.en: Its opposite in land management is drain, which takes water out instead of in.
normal.cn: 它在土地管理中的反义是 drain，把水排出而不是引入。

abstract.en: Picture a gate raised two inches and the water front crawling up the dry ditch.
abstract.cn: 想象闸板抬高两寸，水头立刻沿着干沟向上爬。

abstract.en: Picture soil changing colour in a line, from pale grey to dark brown.
abstract.cn: 想象土壤沿一条线变色，由浅灰转为深褐。

abstract.en: Picture a wound being cleaned by a thin steady stream, not by a splash.
abstract.cn: 想象一道伤口被细而稳的液流清洁，而不是被泼溅。

examples.en: Farmers irrigate the rice fields twice a week in the dry season.
examples.cn: 旱季里农民每周给稻田浇两次水。

examples.en: The surgeon irrigated the wound with saline before stitching.
examples.cn: 外科医生在缝合前用盐水冲洗伤口。

examples.en: A single river can irrigate a whole valley if its water is led by canals.
examples.cn: 只要用渠道引水，一条河就能灌溉整条山谷。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ir-（进入）+ rig（浇水）+ -ate（动词）」——把水引进去 → 灌溉、浇灌

root: 拉丁 in-「进入」+ rigare「浇水、润湿」→ irrigare「引水入、浇灌」；rigare 更早来源不确定。英语经法语与晚期拉丁进入。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the plain act to its methods and borrowings: watering crops, leading water by channels, flushing a wound and then a cavity, a river watering its banks, making dry land farmable, moistening anything, and watering turf for use.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从朴素的行为走向其方式与借用：浇灌作物、用渠道引水、冲洗伤口再到冲洗体腔、河流浸润两岸、使旱地可耕、把任何东西弄湿，以及为使用而给草坪供水。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand lifting a gate so that water begins to move along a dry channel.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手提起闸门，水开始沿着干涸的渠道流动。

branches.en: THE BASIC ACT AND ITS CHANNEL: giving water, and the ditches that decide where it goes.
branches.cn: 基本行为与其通道：给水，以及决定水流去向的沟渠。

branches.en: MEDICAL FLUSH: the same directed stream cleans a wound, then a hollow organ.
branches.cn: 医学冲洗：同一股定向液流先清洁伤口，再清洁中空器官。

branches.en: THE RIVER'S OWN WORK: no pump, no engineer, just water reaching the bank.
branches.cn: 河流自己的工作：没有水泵，没有工程师，只有水抵达河岸。

branches.en: LAND MADE PRODUCTIVE: watering changes what dry ground can grow.
branches.cn: 土地变得可耕：供水改变了旱地能种什么。

branches.en: MOISTURE AND UPKEEP: from making anything damp to keeping turf green for use.
branches.cn: 湿润与养护：从把任何东西弄湿，到为使用而让草坪常绿。

intro.en: Irrigate can be read in parts: an assimilated Latin prefix, the Latin root of watering, and a verb ending.
intro.cn: irrigate 可按部分读出：一个同化的拉丁前缀、表示浇水的拉丁词根，以及一个动词词尾。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is real: irrigare, irrigatio, irrigator and irrigabilis all descend from the same verb, with rigare as the watering root.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词族是真实的：irrigare、irrigatio、irrigator 与 irrigabilis 都出自同一个动词，rigare 是其中的浇水词根。

items.structure: Latin in- 'into', assimilated to ir- before r
items.example: The prefix sends the water into the field.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把水送入田里。

items.example: The root is shared with irrigation and irrigator.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根与 irrigation 和 irrigator 共用。

items.example: The ending turns the root into a working verb.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把词根变成可用的动词。

items.example: Adding the suffix yields irrigation.
items.exampleCN: 加上这个后缀就得到 irrigation。

items.example: Irrigator names the person or the device.
items.exampleCN: irrigator 指那个人或那个器具。

items.example: Irrigable land can take water.
items.exampleCN: irrigable 指可以受水的土地。

items.example: Irrigation supplies the fields in summer.
items.exampleCN: 灌溉在夏天为田地供水。

items.meaning: one who or that which irrigates
items.example: The irrigator repairs the channel gates.
items.exampleCN: 灌溉者修理渠口的闸门。

items.example: Only half the valley is irrigable.
items.exampleCN: 这条山谷只有一半可以灌溉。

items.example: Irrigational canals cross the plain.
items.exampleCN: 灌溉渠道横穿平原。

latinEntries.meaning: to lead water in, to water

latinEntries.structure: Latin noun of action from irrigare
latinEntries.meaning: a watering, a supplying of water

definition_zh: 口头传统；以口耳相传代代延续的故事、歌谣与知识；口述史研究中的口头资料体系
definition_en: the body of stories, songs and knowledge that a community passes on by speech rather than by writing
core_image: 火堆旁，老人开口讲起，孩子跟着复述，同一段故事在每一代人嘴里略微改变
scene: 火堆旁，老人把祖辈的故事讲给围坐的孩子，孩子第二天又学着讲给更小的孩子听。 An oral tradition kept the story alive without a single written page.
sceneCN: 这里 oral tradition 指以口耳相传延续的故事与知识（第 1 个义项：作为整体传统）；句意为口头传统让这个故事一页纸都没写也活了下来。

pos.zh: 口头传统（可数，指某一群体的传统；不可数，指这种传承方式）

derivatives.zh: 口头地（由基础形容词加表方式的副词后缀而来，由形容词转指方式）
传统的（由基础名词加表属性的形容词后缀而来，由名词转指性质）
传统主义（由基础形容词加表主张的名词后缀而来，由性质转指主张）
传统主义者（由基础形容词加表主张者的名词后缀而来，由主张转指持主张的人）

senses.title: The transmitted body
senses.definition: the whole body of stories, songs, laws and knowledge a community hands on by speech
senses.definitionCN: 一个群体靠言谈代代传下的故事、歌谣、规矩与知识的总和
senses.example: The village's oral tradition includes songs that no book records.
senses.exampleCN: 这个村子的口头传统里有任何书都没有记录的歌。
senses.why: Tradition is what is handed over; oral fixes the medium. Together they name a body of material, not a single telling.
senses.whyCN: 前者指被递交下来的东西，后者限定媒介；合起来命名的是一批材料，而非某一次讲述。

senses.title: The medium itself
senses.definition: transmission through voice and memory instead of writing
senses.definitionCN: 依靠嗓音与记忆而不是文字来传递的方式
senses.example: The epic survived for centuries through oral tradition alone.
senses.exampleCN: 这部史诗仅靠口头传统就流传了几个世纪。
senses.why: Here the phrase names the channel rather than the content: speech, memory and repetition do the work of a book.
senses.whyCN: 这里命名的不是内容而是通道：言谈、记忆与复述承担了书本的工作。

senses.title: A family's or clan's account
senses.definition: the particular version of events that one lineage recites about its own past
senses.definitionCN: 某一世系关于自身过去的特定讲述版本
senses.example: His family's oral tradition places the first ancestor in the northern hills.
senses.exampleCN: 他家口头传下的说法把最早的祖先放在北边的山里。
senses.why: Every group keeps its own version; the phrase can narrow from a whole culture to one family's handed-down account.
senses.whyCN: 每个群体都保留自己的版本；这个词组可以从整个文化收窄到一户人家的口传说法。

senses.title: Oral history as method
senses.definition: recorded interviews and testimony used by historians as evidence
senses.definitionCN: 历史学者用作证据的录音访谈与证言
senses.example: Her research combines oral tradition with colonial tax records.
senses.exampleCN: 她的研究把口述材料与殖民时期的税册结合起来。
senses.why: Once a tape recorder is added, spoken memory becomes an archive; the phrase then names a research method.
senses.whyCN: 一旦加上录音机，口传记忆就变成档案；这个词组于是命名一种研究方法。

senses.title: Customary law recited
senses.definition: rules that are remembered and spoken aloud rather than written in a code
senses.definitionCN: 靠记忆与当众诵说、而非写成法典的规则
senses.example: The elders settled the dispute according to oral tradition.
senses.exampleCN: 长老们依照口传的习惯法解决了这场纠纷。
senses.why: Law can live in trained memory; where no code exists, the same phrase covers the binding rules of the community.
senses.whyCN: 法律可以活在受过训练的记忆里；在没有法典的地方，这个词组覆盖群体内有约束力的规则。

senses.title: Oral poetry and performance
senses.definition: verse composed and re-performed aloud with formulaic phrases and music
senses.definitionCN: 以套语与音乐在口头创作并反复表演的韵文
senses.example: Homeric oral tradition was built on repeated epithets and fixed metres.
senses.exampleCN: 荷马式的口头传统建立在重复的修饰语与固定格律之上。
senses.why: In performance the text is recreated each time, so the phrase also names a poetic technique rather than a mere source.
senses.whyCN: 在表演中文本每次都被重新创造，因此这个词组也命名一种诗歌技艺，而不只是素材来源。

senses.title: The stage before writing
senses.definition: the period in a culture's history when knowledge circulated only by speech
senses.definitionCN: 一个文化史上知识只靠言谈流通的时期
senses.example: Scholars debate what oral tradition preserved before the first scripts.
senses.exampleCN: 学者们争论在最早的文字之前口头传统保存了什么。
senses.why: The phrase can mark a chronological stage, set against the moment a society begins to write.
senses.whyCN: 这个词组可以标记一个时间阶段，与社会开始书写的时刻相对。

senses.title: The reliability debate
senses.definition: the argument over whether spoken memory can be trusted as historical evidence
senses.definitionCN: 关于口头记忆能否作为历史证据被信任的争论
senses.example: The reliability debate treats oral tradition as testimony to be tested, not dismissed.
senses.exampleCN: 可靠性之争把口头传统当作有待检验的证言，而不是一概否定。
senses.why: Because memory reshapes what it keeps, the phrase also names the scholarly quarrel about its evidential value.
senses.whyCN: 因为记忆会重塑它所保存的东西，这个词组也命名关于其证据价值的学术争论。

intro.en: Oral comes from Latin os 'mouth' through oralis; tradition comes from Latin traditio 'a handing over', from tradere 'to hand across'. The English phrase was fixed as a folklore term in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: oral 经拉丁 oralis 来自 os「嘴」；tradition 来自拉丁 traditio「递交」，源自动词 tradere「交过去」。这个英语词组在十八、十九世纪作为民俗学术语固定下来。年代均为约数。

items.en: Os (genitive oris) meant 'mouth'. Oralis 'of the mouth' gave English oral. The deeper origin of os is not established.
items.cn: os（属格 oris）意为「嘴」。oralis「嘴的」给出英语 oral。os 更深的来源未得到证明。

items.en: Tradere 'to hand over, deliver, betray' is transparently trans- 'across' plus dare 'to give'.
items.cn: tradere「递交、交付、出卖」由表示「穿过」的前缀加 dare「给」构成，结构清楚。

items.en: Traditio named the act of handing something over, and already meant the teaching passed from one generation to the next.
items.cn: traditio 指递交的动作，并且已经表示一代传给下一代的教学内容。

items.en: Old French tradicion carried the word into English in the twelfth and thirteenth centuries, spelling it first with -cioun.
items.cn: 古法语 tradicion 在十二、十三世纪把该词带入英语，早期拼作 -cioun 结尾。

items.en: From the eighteenth century, oral tradition became a standard label for material circulating by speech, as antiquarians began to collect ballads and tales.
items.cn: 从十八世纪起，oral tradition 成为靠言谈流通的材料的标准标签，古物研究者开始收集歌谣与故事。

items.en: Source uncertain: the pre-Latin origin of os is unknown, and the exact date at which the English pairing became a fixed term cannot be pinned down.
items.cn: 来源不确定：os 在拉丁语之前的来源不明，英语这一搭配固定为术语的确切年代也无法确定。

note.en: Group one is about sound and spelling confusions; group two holds neighbours in folklore and history.
note.cn: 第一组是读音与拼写上的混淆；第二组是民俗学与史学中的近邻词。

entries.definition: Of the ear or hearing. It sounds exactly like oral but refers to ears, not mouths.
entries.definitionCN: 关于耳朵或听觉的。读音与 oral 完全相同，却指耳朵，不指嘴。

entries.definition: Spoken rather than written; alone it can describe an exam, a report or a medicine taken by mouth.
entries.definitionCN: 口头的而非书面的；单用时也可指口试、口头报告或口服药物。

entries.definition: Anything handed down; alone it does not say whether the channel was speech or writing.
entries.definitionCN: 任何被传下来的东西；单用时并不说明通道是口说还是书写。

entries.definition: One who hands over something to an enemy. It descends from the same Latin verb 'to hand over' but took the meaning of betrayal.
entries.definitionCN: 把东西交给敌人的人。它源出同一个表示「递交」的拉丁动词，却走上了「背叛」一义。

entries.definition: Recorded personal testimony gathered by interview; it is the modern, documented end of the same field.
entries.definitionCN: 通过访谈采集并录音的个人证言；它是同一领域里现代且有记录的一端。

entries.definition: The tales, beliefs and customs of a people, whether or not they are told orally.
entries.definitionCN: 一个民族的故事、信仰与习俗，不论是否以口说方式讲述。

entries.definition: The activity of telling stories; it names the performance, not the inherited body.
entries.definitionCN: 讲故事的活动；它命名表演行为，而非继承下来的整体。

entries.definition: A near variant stressing speech; oral tradition is the established scholarly term.
entries.definitionCN: 强调口语的近义变体；oral tradition 才是学界固定术语。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Latin parts, real folklore terms and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁构件、真实的民俗学术语与真实的固定说法。

normal.en: Oral points at the mouth; aural points at the ear; the two are pronounced alike, so spelling decides.
normal.cn: oral 指向嘴，aural 指向耳；两词读音相同，靠拼写分辨。

normal.en: Tradition is a handing over: the same Latin verb gives traitor, one who hands something to the enemy.
normal.cn: tradition 是递交：同一个拉丁动词还给出 traitor，即把东西交给敌人的人。

normal.en: The phrase needs no writing at all: voice, memory and repetition are the whole apparatus.
normal.cn: 这个词组完全不需要文字：嗓音、记忆与复述就是全部装置。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the field: preserve an oral tradition, pass down by oral tradition, oral tradition and written record.
normal.cn: 固定说法划出领域：保存口头传统、通过口头传统传下来、口头传统与书面记录。

normal.en: The plural oral traditions is common when different communities are compared.
normal.cn: 比较不同群体时，复数 oral traditions 很常用。

abstract.en: Picture a story that has no original, only a chain of tellers each handing it to the next.
abstract.cn: 想象一个没有原件的故事，只有一串讲述者，每人把它交给下一位。

abstract.en: Picture memory as a room that rearranges the furniture every time someone walks through.
abstract.cn: 想象记忆是一间屋子，每次有人走过，家具就被重新摆一遍。

abstract.en: Picture a library whose shelves are other people's heads.
abstract.cn: 想象一座图书馆，它的书架是别人的脑袋。

examples.en: The oral tradition preserved the names of the first settlers for six generations.
examples.cn: 口头传统把最早定居者的名字保存了六代。

examples.en: Fieldworkers recorded an oral tradition that was already fading.
examples.cn: 田野工作者记录下了一种正在消逝的口头传统。

examples.en: Written law replaced oral tradition only gradually in the highlands.
examples.cn: 在高地，成文法只是逐渐取代了口头传统。

dict_mnemonic.text: oral（嘴的）+ tradition（递交）＝ 用嘴一代代交下去的东西；记「不落纸，只落嘴」。

root: oral 源自拉丁 os「嘴」，属格为 oris，更早来源不确定，经形容词 oralis 进入英语；tradition 源自拉丁 traditio「递交」，来自动词 tradere，该动词由前缀表「穿过」加 dare「给」构成。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses track the same voice from a whole culture's inheritance down to a single family's version, then to method, law, performance, chronology and the argument over evidence.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着同一个嗓音展开：从整个文化的继承，到一户人家的版本，再到方法、法律、表演、时间阶段与证据之争。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a voice in firelight handing a story to the next pair of ears.
core.cn: 核心意象：火光里的一个嗓音，把故事交给下一双耳朵。

branches.en: BODY AND CHANNEL: what is handed on, and the speaking that hands it on.
branches.cn: 整体与通道：被交下来的是什么，以及交它的言说方式。

branches.en: ONE LINEAGE'S VERSION: the same channel narrowed to a family's own account.
branches.cn: 一个世系的版本：同一通道收窄为一户人家的说法。

branches.en: TAPE RECORDER: spoken memory becomes evidence once it is recorded and cited.
branches.cn: 录音机：口传记忆一旦被录下并引用，就成了证据。

branches.en: BINDING RULES AND EARLY TIME: recitation can hold law, and the phrase can mark the age before writing.
branches.cn: 有约束力的规则与早期时段：诵说可以承载法律，这个词组也能标记文字之前的年代。

branches.en: PERFORMANCE AND DOUBT: the poem is recreated each telling, which is exactly why its reliability is argued.
branches.cn: 表演与怀疑：诗在每次讲述中都被重新创造，这也正是其可靠性被争论的原因。

intro.en: The phrase is a modern English combination of two Latin borrowings, one naming the mouth and one naming the act of handing over.
intro.cn: 这个词组是两个拉丁借词的现代英语组合，一个命名嘴，一个命名递交的动作。

latinIntro.en: Latin os, oralis and traditio, tradere supply every morpheme in the phrase; no Greek element is involved.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 os、oralis 与 traditio、tradere 提供了词组中的全部语素，不涉及希腊成分。

definition_zh: 地球科学（研究地球系统及其岩石、水、大气与生命的学科群）
definition_en: the sciences that study the earth as a system, including its rocks, water, air and life
core_image: 一颗星球被切成剖面：岩石、水、空气与生物各占一圈，旁边摆着测量仪器

sceneCN: 这里 earth science 指「研究地球各圈层的学科」（第 1 个义项：地球科学总称）；句意为一门地球科学课程让学生每次暴雨后去测量河流流量。图中可辨识物件：流速仪、河岸标尺、卫星图、雨后的浑水。

senses.title: The family of sciences about the earth
senses.titleCN: 研究地球的学科群总称
senses.definition: the group of disciplines that study the solid earth, its water, air, climate and living cover
senses.definitionCN: 研究固体地球、其水体、大气、气候与生命覆盖层的学科群
senses.example: A course in earth science sends students to measure stream flow after every storm.
senses.exampleCN: 一门地球科学课程让学生每次暴雨后去测量河流流量。
senses.why: Earth is the native English word for the planet and science is the Latin-derived word for organised knowledge, so the phrase simply names knowledge about the earth.
senses.whyCN: earth 是英语本族词「地球」，science 是拉丁来源的「系统知识」，因此这个短语就是「关于地球的知识」。

senses.title: A school or university subject
senses.titleCN: 中小学或大学的课程科目
senses.definition: a taught subject that combines geology, weather, oceans and space science for students
senses.definitionCN: 为学生把地质、气象、海洋与空间科学结合起来的教学科目
senses.example: Earth science is required for graduation in this district.
senses.exampleCN: 在这个学区，地球科学是毕业必修课。
senses.why: Schools group the branches into one timetable slot, so the phrase also names a course rather than a research field.
senses.whyCN: 学校把各分支合并进一个课表位置，因此这个短语也指课程，而不只是研究领域。

senses.title: The set of its branches
senses.definition: the collection of fields such as geology, meteorology, oceanography and hydrology
senses.definitionCN: 地质学、气象学、海洋学与水文学等领域的集合
senses.example: The department lists four branches of earth science in its catalogue.
senses.exampleCN: 该系在课程目录中列出地球科学的四个分支。
senses.why: Because the phrase is plural in meaning, it can stand for the list of disciplines it contains.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个短语在意义上是复数，它可以指它所包含的那一串学科。

senses.title: Its field and laboratory methods
senses.definition: the practices of observation, sampling, remote sensing and modelling used to study the earth
senses.definitionCN: 研究地球所用的观测、采样、遥感与建模等做法
senses.example: Earth science methods now depend heavily on satellite data.
senses.exampleCN: 地球科学方法如今严重依赖卫星数据。
senses.why: A science is also a set of methods, and the phrase can name those methods as a body of practice.
senses.whyCN: 一门科学也是一套方法，这个短语可以指作为一整套实践的那些方法。

senses.title: Pre-college earth science education
senses.definition: the teaching of earth processes to young students as part of general science
senses.definitionCN: 作为普通科学的一部分，向低龄学生教授地球过程
senses.example: Earth science education now includes local flood history.
senses.exampleCN: 地球科学教育如今纳入本地的洪水史。
senses.why: The phrase labels a curriculum area as well as a research discipline, and teaching is the clearest example.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语既标记研究学科，也标记课程领域，而教学是最清楚的例子。

senses.title: Data about the earth system
senses.titleCN: 关于地球系统的数据与资料
senses.definition: measurements and archives of the earth's surface, interior, oceans and atmosphere
senses.definitionCN: 关于地球表面、内部、海洋与大气的测量与档案
senses.example: Open earth science data let schools run their own climate projects.
senses.exampleCN: 开放的地球科学数据让学校开展自己的气候项目。
senses.why: Modern fields are identified by their data as much as their questions, so the phrase attaches to datasets.
senses.whyCN: 现代领域既由问题定义，也由数据定义，因此这个短语附着于数据集。

senses.title: An academic department or agency
senses.definition: an institutional unit that groups earth-focused researchers and teaching
senses.definitionCN: 把以地球为对象的研究者与教学集中在一起的机构单位
senses.example: The earth science department shares a building with the chemistry lab.
senses.exampleCN: 地球科学系与化学实验室共用一栋楼。
senses.why: Institutions need a collective label, and this phrase is the usual one for a department or survey agency.
senses.whyCN: 机构需要一个集体标签，而这个短语就是院系或调查机构常用的那一个。

senses.title: The integrated view of the earth as a system
senses.titleCN: 把地球当作系统的整合视角
senses.definition: the approach that treats rock, water, air, ice and life as one interacting system rather than separate subjects
senses.definitionCN: 把岩石、水、空气、冰与生命当作一个相互作用系统、而非分开科目的取向
senses.example: Earth science treats rock, water, air, ice and life as one interacting system.
senses.exampleCN: 地球科学把岩石、水、空气、冰与生命视为一个相互作用的系统。
senses.why: The plural branches were later reunified under a systems view, which the phrase can also carry.
senses.whyCN: 原本分开的各分支后来在系统视角下重新统一，这个短语也能承载这一层。

intro.en: Earth science is a modern English compound of two very different words: earth, from Old English eorþe, and science, from Latin scientia 'knowledge'. The phrase has no single coiner and its first date is uncertain.
intro.cn: earth science 是近代英语复合词，由两个来源很不同的词构成：earth 来自古英语 eorþe，science 来自拉丁 scientia「知识」。这个短语没有单一首创者，确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Eorþe meant 'earth, ground, soil'. It descends from a reconstructed Proto-Germanic form and has no Latin root; the deeper Indo-European origin is debated.
items.cn: eorþe 意为「大地、地面、土壤」，来自重构的原始日耳曼语形式，没有拉丁词根；更深的印欧来源有争议。

items.en: Scientia meant 'knowledge', from scire 'to know'. English science entered through Old French in the Middle Ages.
items.cn: scientia 意为「知识」，来自 scire「知道」。英语 science 在中世纪经古法语进入。

items.en: In the seventeenth century science narrowed from 'knowledge' in general to organised, methodical study of nature.
items.cn: 十七世纪，science 从泛指的「知识」收窄为对自然的有组织、有方法的研究。

items.en: Earth science as a collective label for geology, meteorology, oceanography and related fields is a nineteenth- and twentieth-century usage; the exact first record is uncertain.
items.cn: earth science 作为地质学、气象学、海洋学及相关领域的集合标签，是十九至二十世纪的用法；确切最早记载不确定。

items.en: In the twentieth century the phrase became a standard school and university subject name, grouping the branches for teaching.
items.cn: 二十世纪，这个短语成为标准的中学与大学科目名，为教学把各分支归并起来。

items.en: Late twentieth-century earth system science reunited the branches under one model of interacting spheres.
items.cn: 二十世纪后期的地球系统科学把各分支重新统一到一个「圈层相互作用」的模型中。

note.en: Group one holds near-identical labels that differ in breadth or structure; group two holds neighbouring fields that study only part of the earth.
note.cn: 第一组是范围或结构不同、名称极近的标签；第二组是只研究地球某一部分的相邻领域。

entries.definition: A learned synonym built on Greek gē; it overlaps heavily with earth science but is commoner in research than in schools.
entries.definitionCN: 以希腊 gē 构成的书面对应词；与 earth science 高度重叠，但在研究界比在学校更常用。

entries.definition: The practitioner, formed with -ist; the field is earth science, the person is an earth scientist.
entries.definitionCN: 从业者，由 -ist 构成；领域是 earth science，人是 earth scientist。

entries.definition: The study of human impact and ecosystems; it borrows earth data but focuses on pollution and policy.
entries.definitionCN: 研究人类影响与生态系统；借用地球数据，但聚焦污染与政策。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning 'made of earth or clay', from earth plus -en; it describes material, not a field of study.
entries.definitionCN: 由 earth 加 -en 构成的形容词，意为「土制的」；描述材料，而非研究领域。

entries.definition: The study of rocks and earth history; it is one branch of earth science, not the whole.
entries.definitionCN: 研究岩石与地球历史；是地球科学的一个分支，而非全部。

entries.definition: The study of landforms, climate and water at the surface; it overlaps earth science but keeps a spatial focus.
entries.definitionCN: 研究地表地貌、气候与水；与地球科学重叠，但保持空间视角。

entries.definition: The systems-oriented branch that models the interactions of rock, water, air, ice and life.
entries.definitionCN: 以系统为取向的分支，建模岩石、水、空气、冰与生命的相互作用。

entries.definition: The study of planets including the earth; it extends beyond the earth, so it is wider in one direction.
entries.definitionCN: 研究包括地球在内的行星；范围向地球之外延伸，因此在另一个方向上更宽。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Earth is the planet and science is organised knowledge: knowledge about the planet.
normal.cn: earth 是行星，science 是有系统的知识：关于这颗行星的知识。

normal.en: The family runs earth, earthly, earth scientist, science, scientific, scientist, geoscience.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 earth、earthly、earth scientist、science、scientific、scientist、geoscience。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: earth science course, earth science data, earth science department.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：地球科学课程、地球科学数据、地球科学系。

normal.en: The plural earth sciences names the branches, while earth science names the whole group.
normal.cn: 复数 earth sciences 指各分支，earth science 则指整个学科群。

normal.en: Earth system science is the integrated view of the same material.
normal.cn: 地球系统科学是对同一批材料的整合视角。

abstract.en: Picture a planet cut open like an orange, each layer labelled.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗像橙子一样被切开的行星，每层都贴了标签。

abstract.en: Picture a classroom whose windows look onto a river gauge.
abstract.cn: 想象一间教室，窗外正对着一条河的水位尺。

abstract.en: Picture four maps of the same place stacked into one.
abstract.cn: 想象同一地方的四张地图叠成一张。

examples.en: A course in earth science sends students to measure stream flow after every storm.
examples.cn: 一门地球科学课程让学生每次暴雨后去测量河流流量。

examples.en: Earth science methods now depend heavily on satellite data.
examples.cn: 地球科学方法如今严重依赖卫星数据。

examples.en: Earth system science asks how melting ice changes the solid ground beneath it.
examples.cn: 地球系统科学追问融冰如何改变其下的大地。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「地球 + 科学」——把整颗星球当成一门课来研究 → 地球科学

root: earth 来自古英语 eorþe（原始日耳曼语来源，无拉丁词根）；science 来自拉丁 scientia「知识」，由 scire「知道」构成。英语短语 earth science 为近代组合，确切首见年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one object: the planet taken as a subject. The object is first the family of fields, then a course, a list of branches, a set of methods, a curriculum, a dataset, a department, and finally a system.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个对象展开：把整颗行星当作一门学问。这个对象先是学科群，再是课程、分支清单、方法、课程领域、数据集、院系，最后是一个系统。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a planet sliced into layers, each labelled and measured.
core.cn: 核心意象：一颗被切成若干层、每层都标注并测量的行星。

branches.en: WHOLE AND PARTS: the collective name and the list of branches it contains.
branches.cn: 整体与部分：集合名称，以及它所包含的分支清单。

branches.en: CLASSROOM: the same label marks a school subject and a curriculum area.
branches.cn: 课堂：同一标签既标记学校科目，也标记课程领域。

branches.en: PRACTICE AND DATA: observation, remote sensing and archives define the field in use.
branches.cn: 实践与数据：观测、遥感与档案在使用中定义这门领域。

branches.en: INSTITUTION: a department or agency carries the name.
branches.cn: 机构：院系或机构以此命名。

branches.en: SYSTEM VIEW: the separate branches reunite into one interacting whole.
branches.cn: 系统视角：分开的各分支重新合成一个相互作用的整体。

intro.en: The phrase joins an Old English noun of the planet to a Latin noun of knowledge, which is why one half feels plain and the other learned.
intro.cn: 这个短语把古英语的「行星」名词与拉丁的「知识」名词连在一起，因此一半朴素，一半书卷。

latinIntro.en: Only the second half is Latin: scientia from scire. Earth is Germanic and has no Latin cognate, so the Latin entries below cover just the science element.
latinIntro.cn: 只有后半部分是拉丁语：scientia 来自 scire。earth 是日耳曼语词，没有拉丁同源词，因此下列拉丁条目只涵盖 science 这一成分。

items.example: Seo eorþe wæs wēt.
items.exampleCN: 土地是湿的。

items.example: The earth turns once a day.
items.exampleCN: 地球每天自转一次。

items.example: Earthly concerns seemed small from orbit.
items.exampleCN: 从轨道上看，尘世的牵挂显得很小。

items.example: Scientia potentia est.
items.exampleCN: 知识就是力量。

items.example: Science tests its claims against evidence.
items.exampleCN: 科学用证据检验其主张。

items.example: The claim lacks scientific support.
items.exampleCN: 这一主张缺乏科学支持。

items.example: The scientist repeated the measurement.
items.exampleCN: 这位科学家重复了测量。

items.example: Earth science covers rock, water and air.
items.exampleCN: 地球科学涵盖岩石、水与空气。

items.example: Geoscience departments often include hydrology.
items.exampleCN: 地球科学系常包含水文学。

definition_zh: 复杂精密的；老练的；有品位的；精密的；世故的；高级的
definition_en: highly developed, complex and refined, or showing worldly experience and cultivated taste
core_image: 掌心大小的设备里叠着十几层电路，工程师用平板展开一张三维结构图
scene: 展厅中央摆着一台只有手掌大的设备，里面却叠着十几层电路，工程师用平板调出三维模型慢慢旋转。 The new spectrometer is sophisticated enough to detect traces of a single element.
sceneCN: 这里指技术构造复杂而精密（第 1 个义项：复杂精密）；句意为这台新光谱仪精密得足以检测出单一元素的微量痕迹。图中可辨识物件：掌上设备、多层电路、平板上的三维模型、展台灯。

pos.zh: 复杂精密的；老练的；有品位的；世故的

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加表示状态的名词词尾构成，义为「精密；老练；品位」
同一词干构成的动词与名词，义为「使复杂精巧」与「老于世故的人」
由否定前缀加本词构成，义为「不复杂的；单纯质朴的」
由形容词加副词词尾构成，义为「精密地；老练地」，较少使用

senses.title: Complex and finely made
senses.definition: of a device, system or method, highly developed with many carefully arranged parts
senses.definitionCN: 指设备、系统或方法高度发展，由许多精心安排的部件组成
senses.example: The new spectrometer is sophisticated enough to detect traces of a single element.
senses.exampleCN: 这台新光谱仪精密得足以检测出单一元素的微量痕迹。
senses.why: The word began as a charge of adulteration and ended as praise of complexity, an inversion worth remembering.
senses.whyCN: 这个词起初指控「掺假」，最后却用来赞美复杂，这一反转值得记住。

senses.title: Worldly and experienced
senses.definition: of a person, experienced in social life and hard to deceive
senses.definitionCN: 指人在社会生活中经验丰富，不易受骗
senses.example: She is sophisticated enough to read the room before she speaks.
senses.exampleCN: 她足够老练，开口之前就能读懂现场气氛。
senses.why: Nineteenth-century English moved the word from mixtures to manners: experience became a kind of refinement.
senses.whyCN: 十九世纪英语把这个词从「混合物」转向「举止」：经验本身成了一种精致。

senses.title: Cultivated in taste
senses.definition: of taste or style, refined and informed rather than crude
senses.definitionCN: 指品味或风格精致有见识，而非粗陋
senses.example: The restaurant offers a sophisticated menu without any fuss.
senses.exampleCN: 这家餐厅提供精致而不张扬的菜单。
senses.why: Taste is the surface where experience becomes visible, so the two senses often appear together.
senses.whyCN: 品味是经验变得可见的表层，因此两种含义常一起出现。

senses.title: Precise in method
senses.definition: of a technique or instrument, accurate and technically advanced
senses.definitionCN: 指技术或仪器准确且技术先进
senses.example: The lab uses sophisticated methods to date the samples.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室用精密的方法为样本测定年代。
senses.why: A method with many carefully arranged steps is complex in the modern, approving sense of the word.
senses.whyCN: 步骤繁多且精心安排的方法，就是这个词现代褒义上的「复杂」。

senses.title: Adulterated, in the old sense
senses.definition: historically, mixed with a foreign substance so as to be impure
senses.definitionCN: 历史上指掺入外来物质而变得不纯
senses.example: The seventeenth-century label warned that the wine was sophisticated.
senses.exampleCN: 十七世纪的标签警告说这酒掺了假。
senses.why: This older sense survives mainly in dictionaries and explains why the modern praise sounds ironic at first.
senses.whyCN: 这个旧义主要留存于词典中，也解释了为何现代的赞美乍听有些反讽。

senses.title: Knowing in the ways of the world
senses.definition: of a view or attitude, shaped by broad experience rather than innocence
senses.definitionCN: 指看法或态度由广泛经验塑造，而非天真
senses.example: He gave a sophisticated account of how the deal was really made.
senses.exampleCN: 他就这笔交易的真实达成方式给出了老于世故的叙述。
senses.why: A view shaped by exposure to many dealings is worldly rather than innocent.
senses.whyCN: 由许多往来塑造的看法，是世故的，而非天真的。

senses.title: Advanced in the market
senses.definition: of a product or market, aimed at demanding and knowledgeable buyers
senses.definitionCN: 指产品或市场面向要求高、懂行的买家
senses.example: The brand moved into a more sophisticated segment last year.
senses.exampleCN: 该品牌去年进入了更高端的市场区间。
senses.why: Complex refinement is also a market position, aimed at buyers who can tell the difference.
senses.whyCN: 复杂的精致也是一种市场定位，面向那些分得出差别的买家。

senses.title: Subtle in reasoning or strategy
senses.definition: of an argument or plan, subtle and carefully constructed
senses.definitionCN: 指论证或计划细致而精心构造
senses.example: The paper offers a sophisticated defense of the policy.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇论文为该政策作了精妙的辩护。
senses.why: An argument with layered steps is complex in the mental sense, where refinement is subtlety.
senses.whyCN: 层层推进的论证在智识意义上是复杂的，在那里精致就是细微。

senses.title: Refined in daily life
senses.definition: of food, decor or habits, showing cultivated and complex preferences
senses.definitionCN: 指食物、陈设或习惯显示出有修养且复杂的偏好
senses.example: Their sophisticated dinner parties never feel formal.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的精致晚宴从不显得拘谨。
senses.why: Cultivated preferences in food and decor are complexity made visible in daily life.
senses.whyCN: 食物与陈设上经修养的偏好，是复杂在日常生活里变得可见。

intro.en: Sophisticated began with Greek wisdom, passed through the figure of the sophist and an old sense of adulteration, and only later became praise for complexity and refinement.
intro.cn: 这个词始于希腊语的「智慧」，经过「智者」这一身份与「掺假」的旧义，后来才变成对复杂与精致的赞美。

items.en: sophos meant wise, skilled, clever; it is the root of philosophy as well.
items.cn: sophos 意为「有智慧、有技艺、聪明」，也是 philosophy 的词根。

items.en: A sophistes was a skilled professional, later a paid teacher of argument, and the word acquired a suspicious tone.
items.cn: sophistes 原指有技艺的专业人士，后来指收费教授论辩的教师，这个词因此带上可疑色彩。

items.en: Latin took the Greek adjective as sophisticus, describing sophist argument and later dishonest mixture.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入希腊形容词作 sophisticus，描述诡辩，后来也指不老实的掺混。

items.en: The verb sophisticare meant to adulterate or tamper with something.
items.cn: 动词 sophisticare 意为「掺假、做手脚」。

items.en: English first used the participle for something adulterated; the first date is approximate but the Greek line is clear.
items.cn: 英语最初用这个分词指被掺假的东西；首见年份为约数，但希腊来源线索清楚。

items.en: By the nineteenth century the word had reversed: worldly experience and complex refinement became the praised qualities.
items.cn: 到十九世纪，这个词发生了反转：世故经验与复杂精致成了被赞美的品质。

note.en: The first group shares the sophos stem or looks close; the second group names nearby kinds of depth, and the note sets it against superficial.
note.cn: 第一组共享 sophos 词干或形音相近；第二组是邻近的深度类说法，说明中把它与 superficial 对照。

entries.definition: The noun for complexity, refinement or worldly knowledge.
entries.definitionCN: 指复杂、精致或世故的知识。

entries.definition: A worldly person, or the verb to make something more complex or refined.
entries.definitionCN: 指老于世故的人，或使某物更复杂精致的动词。

entries.definition: Simple and plain, sometimes in a good way and sometimes as a criticism.
entries.definitionCN: 指简单朴素，有时是褒义，有时是批评。

entries.definition: Relating to sophists or to clever but misleading argument.
entries.definitionCN: 指与智者派有关的，或指巧辩而误导的论证。

entries.definition: Pretentious and immature; it joins the wise root to a root for fool.
entries.definitionCN: 指自命不凡又幼稚；把「智慧」词根与「愚人」词根接在一起。

entries.definition: Purified and polished in taste or manners; it stresses the removal of what is coarse.
entries.definitionCN: 指品味或举止经提纯打磨；强调去掉粗陋。

entries.definition: Far along in development; it stresses technical progress, not social polish.
entries.definitionCN: 指发展程度高；强调技术进步，而非社交修养。

entries.definition: Developed through training and education, especially in a person's mind or taste.
entries.definitionCN: 指经由训练与教育发展而成，尤指心智或品味。

entries.definition: Experienced in practical affairs; it stresses exposure rather than refinement.
entries.definitionCN: 指在实际事务中有经验；强调阅历，而非精致。

entries.definition: Staying on the surface without depth; in judgments of knowledge or taste it is the opposite pole.
entries.definitionCN: 指停留在表面、没有深度；在评价知识与品味时是相反一极。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Greek wisdom root, the real inversion from adulteration to refinement, and the real contrast with superficial.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的希腊「智慧」词根、真实的「掺假到精致」反转，以及与 superficial 的真实对照。

normal.en: Sophos means wise: sophisticated things and people carry a long history of skill and knowledge.
normal.cn: sophos 意为「智慧」：精致的事物与人身上带着悠久的技艺与知识史。

normal.en: The word once meant tampered with; remember the reversal and the modern praise will feel earned.
normal.cn: 这个词曾经意为「被做手脚」；记住这次反转，现代的赞美就显得有来历。

normal.en: Sophisticated technology, sophisticated audience and sophisticated design are three real phrases.
normal.cn: 精密技术、有见识的观众与精致的设计是三个真实搭配。

normal.en: Sophistication is the noun, unsophisticated is the plain opposite, and both keep the wisdom stem.
normal.cn: sophistication 是名词，unsophisticated 是朴素的反面，两者都保留「智慧」词干。

normal.en: Superficial stops at the face; sophisticated goes into the layers behind it.
normal.cn: superficial 停在脸面；sophisticated 走进脸面后面的层。

abstract.en: Complexity is not virtue by itself; a sophisticated lie is still a lie.
abstract.cn: 复杂本身不是美德；一个精密的谎言仍然是谎言。

abstract.en: The word's history warns that polish can be a form of tampering, and that the two meanings never fully separate.
abstract.cn: 这个词的历史提醒：打磨也可能是做手脚，两种含义从未完全分开。

abstract.en: Sophistication is what experience looks like when it has been shaped into taste.
abstract.cn: 精致是经验被塑造成品味之后的模样。

examples.en: The new hearing aid uses sophisticated software to separate speech from noise.
examples.cn: 这款新助听器用精密软件把语音与噪声分开。

examples.en: She moved through the reception with the ease of a sophisticated host.
examples.cn: 她以老练主人的从容穿梭在招待会上。

examples.en: The argument is sophisticated but rests on one unproven assumption.
examples.cn: 这个论证很精妙，却建立在一个未经证明的假设上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「索菲斯提给提德」——从「智者」到「掺假」再到「精致」，一路翻转

root: 来自希腊语 sophos「智慧」→ sophistes「智者」→ sophistikos，经拉丁语 sophisticus 与中世纪拉丁语 sophisticare「掺假」构成分词，十七世纪英语先指「掺假的」，十九世纪转为「世故、精致」。来源链清楚，首见年份为约数。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses run from complex machinery through worldly experience, taste, precise methods, the old adulterated sense, worldliness, high-end markets, subtle argument and refined living.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从复杂机械，经过世故经验、品味、精密方法、旧有的掺假义、通晓世情、高端市场、精妙论证，最后到精致生活。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a palm-sized device holds a dozen stacked circuit layers, opened into a turning model on a tablet.
core.cn: 核心意象：掌心大小的设备里叠着十几层电路，在平板上展开成旋转的模型。

branches.en: THE MACHINE: complex construction and precise method.
branches.cn: 机器：复杂构造与精密方法。

branches.en: THE PERSON: social experience and a knowing view of the world.
branches.cn: 人：社会经验与通晓世情的看法。

branches.en: THE TASTE: refined style in food, decor and daily habits.
branches.cn: 品味：食物、陈设与日常习惯中的精致风格。

branches.en: THE OLD CHARGE: the historical sense of something tampered with.
branches.cn: 旧日指控：历史上「被做手脚」的含义。

branches.en: THE MARKET AND THE ARGUMENT: a high-end segment and a subtle case.
branches.cn: 市场与论证：高端区间与精妙的论辩。

intro.en: Sophisticated is a Greek wisdom stem, a Latin verb of tampering, and an English participle ending that still carries both histories.
intro.cn: 这个词是一个希腊「智慧」词干、一个拉丁「做手脚」动词，和一个仍带着两段历史的英语分词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Greek supplies sophos and sophistes; Latin supplies sophisticus and sophisticare, and English builds the participle on the Latin stem.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语提供了 sophos 与 sophistes；拉丁语提供了 sophisticus 与 sophisticare，英语在拉丁词干上构成分词。

items.example: The root names wisdom.
items.exampleCN: 词根命名智慧。

items.example: The professional figure carries the root.
items.exampleCN: 这一职业身份承载词根。

items.example: The adjective adds argument.
items.exampleCN: 形容词加上论辩色彩。

items.example: Latin borrows the Greek adjective.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语借入希腊形容词。

items.example: The verb supplies the old charge.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供旧日的指控。

items.example: It forms the past participle.
items.exampleCN: 它构成过去分词。

items.example: The word reverses its old charge.
items.exampleCN: 这个词反转了旧日的指控。

items.example: The noun adds a state ending.
items.exampleCN: 名词加上状态词尾。

items.example: It forms unsophisticated, the plain case.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 unsophisticated，即朴素的情形。

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加状态名词词尾构成，义为「精致；老练」
同词干动词与名词，义为「使精巧」与「老于世故者」

由形容词加副词词尾构成，义为「精密地」

definition_zh: 合适地；恰当地；得体地；适度地；合乎规定地
definition_en: in a way that is suitable for a particular purpose, person, or occasion; in a proper or fitting manner
core_image: 把一把钥匙对准它自己的锁孔：只属于这里，也只适合这里
scene: 这里指「合适地」。 A guest in a dark suit waits until the bride's father finishes his speech, then raises a glass at exactly the right moment and says a few short words; a clock on the wall shows the hour. He acts appropriately, raising his glass only when the speech ends.
sceneCN: 这里 appropriately 是「得体地、恰合时宜地」（第 2 个义项：在社交场合举止合乎礼数）；句意：他举止得体，等演讲结束才举杯。图中可辨识物件：深色西装、酒杯、婚礼长桌、正在讲话的父亲、时钟。

senses.title: Suitable for the purpose: the right tool for the task
senses.definition: in a way that suits the purpose or function of something
senses.definitionCN: 以适合某物目的或功能的方式
senses.example: The shelves were appropriately sized for the narrow alcove.
senses.exampleCN: 这些搁板做得正好适合那个窄壁龛。
senses.why: Appropriare is ad- 'to' plus proprius 'one's own': to make a thing one's own, then to set it apart for a use. What is set apart for a use fits that use, so the adverb says the action matches its purpose.
senses.whyCN: appropriare 是 ad-“向”加 proprius“自己的”：使某物成为自己的，再把它拨出来专供某用。被拨给某用途的东西就与那用途相称，因此副词表示“做某事合乎其目的”。

senses.title: Socially proper: behaving as the occasion expects
senses.titleCN: 合乎礼数：举止符合场合期待
senses.definition: in a polite or socially correct way, as the situation requires
senses.definitionCN: 以礼貌或符合社会规范的方式，符合情境要求
senses.example: The children were appropriately quiet during the ceremony.
senses.exampleCN: 仪式期间，孩子们安静得很得体。
senses.why: The 'making one's own' root turns outward: a person takes on the manners that belong to the occasion. What is proper to the room becomes proper in the person, and the adverb names that fit.
senses.whyCN: “使成为自己的”这一词根转向外部：一个人把属于这个场合的举止接纳为自己的。属于这个房间的礼数，变成这个人身上的得体，副词命名的正是这种贴合。

senses.title: Fitting the context: the response matches the situation
senses.titleCN: 贴合情境：回应与局面相称
senses.definition: in a way that matches the particular circumstances, facts, or mood of a situation
senses.definitionCN: 以符合某一情境的具体情况、事实或情绪的方式
senses.example: When the plan changed, she appropriately revised the whole schedule.
senses.exampleCN: 计划一变，她就相应地改了整个日程。
senses.why: The fit is now between an action and a changing situation. Since the appropriate response belongs to that situation, acting appropriately is acting as the case itself demands.
senses.whyCN: 这里的贴合发生在“行动”与“变化的情境”之间。恰当的回应属于那个情境，因此 appropriately 行动，就是按事情本身的要求行动。

senses.title: In due proportion: neither too much nor too little
senses.definition: to a proper or moderate degree, in proportion to what is needed
senses.definitionCN: 达到恰当或适中的程度，与所需成比例
senses.example: The sauce was appropriately seasoned, not oversalted.
senses.exampleCN: 酱汁调味适度，没有过咸。
senses.why: Proprius also carries the idea of what belongs to a thing's own measure. A proper share is the share that belongs to the case, so the adverb can regulate degree: enough, and not more than enough.
senses.whyCN: proprius 还带有“属于某物自身尺度”的意思。恰当的份额，就是属于这个情形的份额，因此副词也能调节程度：足够，但不超过。

senses.title: Assigned to its proper use: allocated rightly
senses.definition: of funds, time, or resources, in a way that assigns them to the use they are meant for
senses.definitionCN: 指资金、时间或资源，以把它们分配给既定用途的方式
senses.example: The grant was appropriately divided between research and training.
senses.exampleCN: 这笔拨款在研究和培训之间分配得当。
senses.why: This is the oldest mechanical sense of appropriare: to set a thing apart for a specific owner or use. Done appropriately, the allocation puts each part where it belongs.
senses.whyCN: 这是 appropriare 最古老的“操作”义：把某物拨出来专供某个所有者或用途。分配得 appropriately，就是把每一部分放到它该在的地方。

senses.title: Suited to a role: the part fits the person
senses.definition: in a way that suits a person's role, rank, or responsibilities
senses.definitionCN: 以适合一个人的角色、身份或职责的方式
senses.example: The new captain appropriately took charge of the evacuation.
senses.exampleCN: 新船长恰如其分地接管了撤离工作。
senses.why: A role is something a person takes as his own. When the person's action belongs to the office he holds, he acts appropriately: the role and the conduct are one fit.
senses.whyCN: 角色是一个人认作自己的东西。当一个人的行为属于他所担任的职位，他就是 appropriately 行动：角色与举止合成一个贴合。

senses.title: Legally or officially proper: within the rules
senses.definition: in accordance with the law, rules, or official procedure
senses.definitionCN: 依照法律、规则或正式程序
senses.example: The documents were appropriately filed with the court.
senses.exampleCN: 这些文件已按规定提交法院备案。
senses.why: What is proper to an institution is what its rules assign to each step. Acting appropriately here means following the procedure that belongs to the case, not merely being polite.
senses.whyCN: 属于一个机构的东西，就是它的规则分配给每个步骤的东西。这里的 appropriately 指遵循属于该案件的程序，而不只是礼貌。

senses.title: Right for the register: words that fit the audience
senses.titleCN: 措辞得体：语言贴合听众
senses.definition: of language, in a style or level of formality that suits the audience and setting
senses.definitionCN: 指语言，以适合听众与场合的风格或正式程度
senses.example: He appropriately avoided slang in the formal report.
senses.exampleCN: 他在正式报告里恰当地避开了俚语。
senses.why: A register is the language that belongs to a setting. Choosing appropriately is choosing the words that are proper to that room, so the social fit becomes a lexical one.
senses.whyCN: 语域是属于某个场合的语言。appropriately 选择，就是选择属于那个房间的词，于是社交上的贴合变成了用词上的贴合。

senses.title: At the right moment: sensible timing and judgment
senses.definition: at a fitting moment or in a sensible way, showing good judgment about when and how to act
senses.definitionCN: 在合适的时刻或以明智的方式，表现出对何时行动、如何行动的良好判断
senses.example: She appropriately waited until the meeting ended before raising the objection.
senses.exampleCN: 她恰当地等到会议结束后才提出异议。
senses.why: Timing is part of what belongs to an occasion: the right act at the wrong moment is not appropriate. The adverb therefore also judges when, fusing suitability with good sense.
senses.whyCN: 时机也是属于一个场合的东西：正确的行为放在错误的时刻就不恰当。因此这个副词也判断“何时”，把合适与明智融在一起。

intro.en: Appropriately is appropriate plus the adverb suffix -ly. The adjective comes from Latin appropriatus, the past participle of appropriare 'make one's own' — ad- 'to' plus proprius 'one's own'. The path runs from taking something as one's own, to setting it apart for a use, to being suitable for that use. Its root is proprius, not pretium (appreciate) and not proximus (approximate).
intro.cn: appropriately 是 appropriate 加副词后缀 -ly。appropriate 来自拉丁语 appropriatus，即 appropriare“使成为自己的”的过去分词——ad-“向”加 proprius“自己的”。路径是：把某物认作自己的 → 把它拨出来专供某用 → 与那用途相称。它的词根是 proprius，不是 appreciate 的 pretium，也不是 approximate 的 proximus。

items.en: The adjective appropriate is first recorded in English meaning 'specially suitable, proper', already carrying the fit-to-purpose sense.
items.cn: 形容词 appropriate 最早记录于英语，义为“特别合适的、恰当的”，已经带有“合乎目的”的意思。

items.en: Appropriate comes from Latin appropriatus, the past participle of appropriare 'make one's own'. The participle frames the word as 'having been made one's own'.
items.cn: appropriate 来自拉丁语 appropriatus，即 appropriare“使成为自己的”的过去分词。分词形式把这个词框定为“已经被认作自己的”。

items.en: Appropriare = ad- 'to' + proprius 'one's own' (the source of proper). To appropriate something is first to take it as your own, then to set it aside for a particular owner or use.
items.cn: appropriare = ad-“向”+ proprius“自己的”（也是 proper 的来源）。appropriate 某物，先是把它认作自己的，再把它拨给某个所有者或用途。

items.en: From 'make one's own' the sense moves to 'assign to a special use', and from there to 'fitting that use'. What belongs to a purpose is what suits it, so ownership turns into suitability.
items.cn: 从“使成为自己的”，词义转到“拨归专门用途”，再转到“与那用途相称”。属于某个目的的东西，就是适合它的东西，于是“所有权”变成了“合适”。

items.en: The English suffix -ly is added to the adjective to form an adverb of manner: suitable becomes 'in a suitable manner'. The suffix adds no new root meaning; it turns the fit into the way an action is done.
items.cn: 英语后缀 -ly 加在形容词后构成方式副词：suitable 变成“以合适的方式”。这个后缀不增加新的词根含义，只是把“相称”变成“行动的方式”。

items.en: Modern English uses appropriately for purpose, manners, context, degree, allocation, roles, rules, register and timing. The base appropriare never meant 'price' or 'nearest'; those belong to appreciate and approximate.
items.cn: 现代英语用 appropriately 表示合乎目的、礼数、情境、适度、分配、角色、规定、语域与时机。词源 appropriare 从来不表示“价格”或“最近”；那些属于 appreciate 与 approximate。

note.en: The first group puts the two false friends (pretium and proximus) beside a true relative; the second group separates appropriately from adverbs that cover only part of its range.
note.cn: 第一组把两个“假朋友”（pretium 与 proximus）放在一个真正的同族词旁边；第二组把 appropriately 与只覆盖其部分范围的副词分开。

entries.definition: to value, be grateful for, or rise in value. It comes from pretium 'price', a root entirely separate from proprius 'one's own'.
entries.definitionCN: 重视；感激；增值。它来自 pretium“价格”，与 proprius“自己的”是完全不同的一套词根。

entries.definition: close to the correct value but not exact. It comes from proximus 'nearest', the third look-alike root that must not be folded into this family.
entries.definitionCN: 接近正确值但不精确的。它来自 proximus“最近的”，是第三个形近词根，绝不能并进这个词族。

entries.definition: the act of setting money or property aside for a use, or of taking it as one's own. It is the noun from appropriate (v.), not the adverb.
entries.definitionCN: 拨款；拨用；挪用；据为己有。它是动词 appropriate 的名词形式，不是副词。

entries.definition: in a way that is right for a purpose or occasion. It is the broadest of the group; appropriately often adds social or moral propriety.
entries.definitionCN: 以适合某目的或场合的方式。它是这一组里最宽泛的；appropriately 往往还加上社交或道德上的得体。

entries.definition: in the correct, accepted, or polite way. It stresses rules and decorum, while appropriately stresses the fit between action and situation.
entries.definitionCN: 以正确、被接受或礼貌的方式。它强调规则与礼仪，而 appropriately 强调行为与情境之间的贴合。

entries.definition: in a way that is apt or becoming, often used of ceremonies and tributes. It is more formal and narrower than appropriately.
entries.definitionCN: 以恰当或相称的方式，常用于仪式与致意。它比 appropriately 更正式，范围也更窄。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: proprius 'one's own', the appropriare family, the adverb suffix -ly, and the fixed phrases appropriately dressed and appropriately named.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：proprius“自己的”、appropriare 词族、副词后缀 -ly，以及 appropriately dressed、appropriately named 等固定搭配。

normal.en: Proprius means 'one's own'. Something appropriate has been made to belong to its purpose, so it fits.
normal.cn: proprius 意为“自己的”。appropriate 的东西已经被认作属于它的目的，因此是合适的。

normal.en: Appropriate is the adjective, -ly makes the adverb: 'suitable' becomes 'in a suitable manner'.
normal.cn: appropriate 是形容词，-ly 把它变成副词：“合适的”变成“以合适的方式”。

normal.en: Appropriately dressed and appropriately named are everyday frames: the clothes or the name matches the person or occasion.
normal.cn: appropriately dressed 与 appropriately named 是日常搭配：衣服或名字与人或场合相配。

normal.en: Appropriation is the noun for money set aside or property taken; it is not the adverb appropriately.
normal.cn: appropriation 是“拨出的款项”或“被占取的财产”的名词，不是副词 appropriately。

normal.en: Appropriately enough is a fixed sentence adverb meaning 'as was fitting', often used for something wryly predictable.
normal.cn: appropriately enough 是固定的句子副词，意为“果然恰如其分”，常用于略带讽刺的“不出所料”。

abstract.en: A key turns only in the lock made for it: the key is not merely good, it belongs to that lock. Appropriately is that one-lock fit.
abstract.cn: 一把钥匙只在为它打造的锁里转动：钥匙不只是好，它属于那把锁。appropriately 就是这种“一把锁的贴合”。

abstract.en: A suit cut for one body hangs badly on another: the same garment can be right here and wrong there.
abstract.cn: 为一个人的身材裁的西装，穿在另一个人身上就别扭：同一件衣服在此处合适，在别处就不合适。

abstract.en: The word judges three things at once: the act, the moment, and the company. Change any one and the fit may fail.
abstract.cn: 这个词同时判断三样东西：行为、时机与在场的人。改动任何一项，贴合都可能失效。

examples.en: She appropriately apologized before the argument could grow.
examples.cn: 在争吵升级之前，她适时地道了歉。

examples.en: The museum appropriately labels each object with its date and origin.
examples.cn: 博物馆恰当地为每件物品标上年代与来源。

examples.en: He was appropriately dressed for the cold chapel, in a heavy coat and gloves.
examples.cn: 他穿着厚外套、戴着手套，正适合那座寒冷的礼拜堂。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿普若普瑞特利」——阿普若（Ap-pro）挑了一件合身的礼服，普瑞（Pu Rui）帮他把领结扶正，特利（Te Li）说：这样出场才得体 → appropriately 合适地、得体地

root: 由 appropriate（源自拉丁语 appropriare“make one's own”，ad- + proprius“自己的”）加副词后缀 -ly 构成，核心是“使成为自己的→拨归专用→与目的相称”，故为合适地、恰当地。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of appropriately all measure one fit: an action and the purpose, occasion, role, rule, register or moment it belongs to. The adverb does not describe the action alone; it describes how well the action sits in its place.
sensesIntro.cn: appropriately 的九个义项都在衡量同一种贴合：一个行为与它所属的目的、场合、角色、规则、语域或时刻是否相配。这个副词不只描述行为本身，更描述行为在它的位置上坐得有多正。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a key that turns only in the lock made for it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把只在为它打造的锁里转动的钥匙。

branches.en: PURPOSE AND CONTEXT: the action suits its task, then suits the changing situation.
branches.cn: 目的与情境：行为先合乎其任务，再合乎变化中的局面。

branches.en: SOCIAL AND LINGUISTIC MANNER: behavior proper to the room, and words proper to the audience.
branches.cn: 社交与语言方式：举止合乎这个房间，用词合乎这批听众。

branches.en: DEGREE AND ALLOCATION: the right share, and resources sent to their proper use.
branches.cn: 程度与分配：恰当的份额，以及资源被送到它该去的用途。

branches.en: ROLE AND RULE: conduct that fits an office, and procedure that fits the law.
branches.cn: 角色与规则：与职位相配的举止，以及与法律相配的程序。

branches.en: TIMING AND JUDGMENT: the right act at the right moment, which is part of the fit.
branches.cn: 时机与判断：正确的行为落在正确的时刻，这也是贴合的一部分。

intro.en: Appropriately is appropriate + -ly, an adverb-of-manner suffix with no root meaning of its own. Appropriate comes from appropriare; English then builds appropriateness, inappropriate, inappropriately, appropriation, misappropriate and misappropriation around the same proprius stem.
intro.cn: appropriately 是 appropriate 加 -ly，后者是构成方式副词的后缀，本身不带来词根含义。appropriate 来自 appropriare；英语随后围绕同一 proprius 词干构造出 appropriateness、inappropriate、inappropriately、appropriation、misappropriate 与 misappropriation。

latinIntro.en: Latin proprius 'one's own, proper' is the direct root. Appropriare 'make one's own' adds ad-, and its participle appropriatus gives the English adjective; proprietas gives the related noun of ownership.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 proprius“自己的、专属的”是直接词根。appropriare“使成为自己的”加了 ad-，其分词 appropriatus 给出英语形容词；proprietas 给出表示所有权的相关名词。

items.meaning: in a fitting or proper way
items.meaningCN: 合适地；恰当地（-ly 构成方式副词）
items.example: The room was appropriately lit for the reading.
items.exampleCN: 这个房间为朗读会打上了恰当的光。

items.meaning: suitable or proper for a purpose
items.meaningCN: 合适的；恰当的（-ate 构成形容词）
items.example: Jeans are not appropriate for the ceremony.
items.exampleCN: 牛仔裤不适合这个仪式。

items.meaning: to set aside for a use, or take as one's own
items.meaningCN: 拨用；挪用；据为己有（同形动词）
items.example: The council appropriated funds for the new library.
items.exampleCN: 议会为新图书馆拨了款。

items.meaningCN: 恰当；得体（-ness 构成状态名词）
items.example: They questioned the appropriateness of the joke.
items.exampleCN: 他们质疑这个笑话是否得体。

items.meaning: not suitable for the purpose or occasion
items.meaningCN: 不合适的；不得体的（in- 表示否定）
items.example: The comment was inappropriate for a public meeting.
items.exampleCN: 那句评论在公开会议上不合适。

items.meaning: in an unsuitable or improper way
items.meaningCN: 不恰当地；不得体地（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: He laughed inappropriately at the bad news.
items.exampleCN: 听到坏消息时，他不合时宜地笑了。

items.meaning: money set aside, or the taking of something as one's own
items.meaningCN: 拨款；拨用；挪用（-ion 构成动作名词）
items.example: The appropriation for road repairs was approved.
items.exampleCN: 道路维修的拨款获批了。

items.meaning: to take money or property dishonestly for one's own use
items.meaningCN: 挪用；侵吞（mis- 表示错误地、不正当地）
items.example: The treasurer misappropriated the club's funds.
items.exampleCN: 司库挪用了俱乐部的资金。

items.meaning: the dishonest taking of funds for one's own use
items.meaningCN: 挪用；侵吞（-ion 构成动作名词）
items.example: The audit revealed misappropriation of the grant.
items.exampleCN: 审计发现了这笔拨款的挪用。

items.meaning: a person who sets something aside or takes it as his own
items.meaningCN: 拨用者；占取者（-or 表示做该动作的人）
items.example: The appropriator of the land was later sued.
items.exampleCN: 占用这块土地的人后来被起诉了。

latinEntries.meaning: one's own, proper, peculiar to a person
latinEntries.meaningCN: 自己的；专属的；某人特有的

latinEntries.meaning: to make one's own, take as one's own
latinEntries.meaningCN: 使成为自己的；据为己有

latinEntries.meaning: made one's own, taken for a use
latinEntries.meaningCN: 已被认作自己的；已被拨用的

definition_zh: 病毒学；研究病毒及其复制、传播与致病的学科
definition_en: the science that studies viruses, their replication, spread, and effects
core_image: 高等级实验室里成排的密封操作箱，屏幕上显示着一段段病毒基因组序列
scene: 这里指「病毒学」。 The department of virology traced the outbreak to a single bat colony.
sceneCN: 这里 virology 是「病毒学」（第 2 个义项：作为院系建制）；句意：病毒学系把这次疫情追溯到一个蝙蝠群落。图中可辨识物件：密封操作箱、基因序列屏幕、采样记录。

pos.zh: 病毒学（不可数名词）；指学科或某一分支，也可指院系建制

derivatives.zh: 病毒学家
病毒学的；病毒学方法的
从病毒学角度地
病毒

senses.title: The Science of Viruses
senses.titleCN: 病毒学：研究病毒的科学
senses.definition: the branch of biology that studies viruses
senses.definitionCN: 生物学中研究病毒的分支
senses.example: Virology asks how a particle with no cell of its own can copy itself.
senses.exampleCN: 病毒学追问一个没有自己细胞的颗粒如何复制自身。
senses.why: Virology joins virus to -logy, the Greek suffix for a disciplined study. Its object is unusual because viruses are not cells, so the science sits at the border of biology.
senses.whyCN: virology 把 virus 与表示系统研究的希腊后缀 -logy 结合；它的对象很特殊，因为病毒不是细胞，所以这门科学处在生物学的边界上。

senses.title: A Discipline and a Department
senses.titleCN: 学科与院系：作为建制单位
senses.definition: the academic field or institutional unit devoted to viruses
senses.definitionCN: 专门研究病毒的学术领域或建制单位
senses.example: The virology department moved into the new safety building.
senses.exampleCN: 病毒学系搬进了新的安全大楼。
senses.why: A field becomes visible when it has a department, a budget and a building. The uncountable name can therefore stand for the institution that practises it.
senses.whyCN: 一个领域有了院系、预算与大楼，才变得可见；因此这个不可数名词可以代指从事它的建制单位。

senses.title: Clinical Virology
senses.titleCN: 临床病毒学：为诊断与治疗服务
senses.definition: the branch that identifies viruses causing human disease
senses.definitionCN: 鉴定引起人类疾病的病毒的分支
senses.example: Clinical virology reported the virus within four hours.
senses.exampleCN: 临床病毒学在四小时内报告了该病毒。
senses.why: In the hospital the science narrows to speed and accuracy: which virus, how much, and which drug. The adjective clinical marks that practical setting.
senses.whyCN: 在医院里，这门科学收窄为速度与准确度：是哪种病毒、有多少、用哪种药；形容词 clinical 标出这一实用场景。

senses.title: Molecular Virology
senses.titleCN: 分子病毒学：研究基因与蛋白机制
senses.definition: the branch that studies viral genomes, proteins and replication at the molecular level
senses.definitionCN: 在分子层面研究病毒基因组、蛋白质与复制的分支
senses.example: Molecular virology explained how the virus enters the cell.
senses.exampleCN: 分子病毒学解释了这种病毒如何进入细胞。
senses.why: The adjective molecular names the level of analysis, not the setting. The same virus can be studied clinically at the bedside or molecularly at the bench.
senses.whyCN: 形容词 molecular 命名的是分析层次，而不是场景；同一种病毒既可在床边做临床研究，也可在实验台上做分子研究。

senses.title: Diagnostic Virology
senses.titleCN: 诊断病毒学：检测与分型
senses.definition: the branch concerned with detecting and typing viruses in samples
senses.definitionCN: 负责在样本中检测病毒并分型的分支
senses.example: Diagnostic virology turned the swab into a typed result.
senses.exampleCN: 诊断病毒学把拭子变成了分型结果。
senses.why: Diagnosis is a distinct job: it does not explain mechanism or treat disease, it answers 'which agent is here'. The adjective isolates that function.
senses.whyCN: 诊断是一项独立工作：它不解释机制，也不治疗疾病，只回答「这里是什么因子」；形容词把这一职能单独标出。

senses.title: Plant and Environmental Virology
senses.titleCN: 植物与环境病毒学：非医学对象
senses.definition: the branches that study viruses of plants or of ecosystems
senses.definitionCN: 研究植物病毒或生态系统中病毒的分支
senses.example: Plant virology saved the orchard by identifying the mosaic virus.
senses.exampleCN: 植物病毒学通过鉴定花叶病毒挽救了果园。
senses.why: Viruses infect far more than humans. The adjective before the field name marks which host group or setting is being studied, and the methods change accordingly.
senses.whyCN: 病毒感染的对象远不止人类；学科名前的形容词标出所研究的宿主群或场景，方法也随之改变。

senses.title: Laboratory Methods
senses.titleCN: 实验室方法：培养、测序与隔离
senses.definition: the practical techniques of culturing, sequencing and handling viruses
senses.definitionCN: 培养、测序与操作病毒的实用技术
senses.example: The course teaches the virology of safe sample handling first.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课首先教授安全处理样本的病毒学操作。
senses.why: Because viruses need living cells, their laboratory handling is unusually demanding. The name can denote that body of technique, not only the theoretical field.
senses.whyCN: 由于病毒需要活细胞，实验室操作的要求异常高；这个名称可以指这套技术本身，而不只是理论领域。

senses.title: The Viruses of a Sample
senses.titleCN: 样本的病毒组成：转喻用法
senses.definition: the viral content or profile found in a sample or a site
senses.definitionCN: 某样本或某地点检出的病毒组成或图谱
senses.example: The virology of the sewage sample matched the clinical cases.
senses.exampleCN: 污水样本的病毒组成与临床病例相符。
senses.why: Specialists say the virology of a sample when they mean the viruses in it. The discipline name stands for its object, the same metonymy seen in microbiology.
senses.whyCN: 专家说某样本的「病毒学」，实际指的是其中的病毒；学科名代替了它的对象，这与微生物学中的转喻相同。

intro.en: Virology is a twentieth-century compound: virus plus -logy, the Greek suffix for a field of study. It became a named science only after viruses could be seen and grown.
intro.cn: virology 是二十世纪的复合词：virus 加 -logy，即表示研究领域的希腊后缀。直到病毒能被看见、能被培养，它才成为一门有名字的科学。

items.en: Latin virus meant 'poison, venom, sap, slimy liquid'. English borrowed it in the late fourteenth century, and the modern sense of a submicroscopic agent was fixed in the 1890s.
items.cn: 拉丁语 virus 意为「毒、毒液、汁液、黏液」；英语于十四世纪末借入，而「亚微观感染因子」的现代义在十九世纪九十年代固定下来。

items.en: Greek -logia came from -log-, the combining form of legein 'to speak, tell', from a root meaning 'to gather, pick out'. The suffix names a disciplined way of speaking about a subject, hence a science.
items.cn: 希腊 -logia 来自 -log-，即 legein「说、讲述」的组合形式，其词根意为「收集、拣选」；该后缀命名关于某主题的一套有纪律的论述方式，因此指一门科学。

items.en: Virology is recorded from 1935, formed from the combining form of virus plus -logy. It arrived after the tobacco mosaic virus and other agents had been isolated and shown to be filterable.
items.cn: virology 记录于 1935 年，由 virus 的组合形式加 -logy 构成；它出现于烟草花叶病毒等因子已被分离、并被证明可通过滤器之后。

items.en: Virologist is recorded from 1946, eleven years later. The delay is typical: a science is named before the people who practise it are named.
items.cn: virologist 记录于 1946 年，晚了十一年；这种滞后很典型：学科先获得名字，从业者随后才有称呼。

items.en: Viruses are smaller than the wavelength of visible light, so they became visible only with the electron microscope. That instrument turned virology from inference into observation.
items.cn: 病毒小于可见光的波长，因此只有电子显微镜才能让它们显现；这件仪器把病毒学从推断变成了观察。

items.en: Molecular virology, diagnostic virology and clinical virology split off as methods matured. Each branch name adds a scope adjective to the same Greek suffix.
items.cn: 随着方法成熟，分子病毒学、诊断病毒学与临床病毒学相继分出；每个分支名都是在同一个希腊后缀前加一个限定范围的形容词。

note.en: The first group separates the field from its practitioner and adjective. The second group holds neighbouring sciences whose objects differ by kind.
note.cn: 第一组区分学科本身与其从业者、形容词；第二组是研究对象按类别相邻的科学。

entries.definition: A person who practises virology. The ending -ist marks the practitioner rather than the field.
entries.definitionCN: 从事病毒学的人；词尾 -ist 标记从业者，而不是学科。

entries.definition: Relating to virology or its methods, as in virological testing. It describes the discipline's procedures, not the virus itself.
entries.definitionCN: 与病毒学或其方法有关的，如病毒学检测；描述的是学科程序，而不是病毒本身。

entries.definition: Of or caused by a virus. It is object-level, while virological is discipline-level.
entries.definitionCN: 指病毒的或由病毒引起的；它是对象层面的形容词，而 virological 是学科层面的。

entries.definition: The study of microorganisms. It often includes viruses by convention, though viruses are not cells, so the two fields overlap at the border.
entries.definitionCN: 研究微生物的学科；按惯例常把病毒算在内，但病毒不是细胞，因此两个领域在边界处重叠。

entries.definition: The study of bacteria, which are cells and can be treated with antibiotics. It is not a branch of virology.
entries.definitionCN: 研究细菌的学科；细菌是细胞，可用抗生素治疗，不属病毒学的分支。

entries.definition: The study of how diseases spread through populations. It asks who, where and when, while virology asks what the agent is.
entries.definitionCN: 研究疾病在人群中如何传播的学科；它问的是谁、何处、何时，而病毒学问的是因子是什么。

entries.definition: The study of the immune system. It studies the host's response to viruses rather than the viruses themselves.
entries.definitionCN: 研究免疫系统的学科；它研究宿主对病毒的反应，而不是病毒本身。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: virus + -logy: the study of viruses, a science named in 1935.
normal.cn: virus + -logy：研究病毒的学问，这门学科于 1935 年得名。

normal.en: The practitioner followed in 1946: first the field, then the virologist.
normal.cn: 从业者的称呼 1946 年才出现：先有领域，后有病毒学家。

normal.en: The family runs virology, virologist, virological, virologically, virus, viral and virion.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 virology、virologist、virological、virologically、virus、viral、virion。

normal.en: Scope adjectives mark the branch: clinical, molecular, diagnostic, plant and environmental virology.
normal.cn: 限定形容词标出分支：临床、分子、诊断、植物与环境病毒学。

normal.en: Viruses are not cells, so virology sits at the edge of biology and often partners with immunology.
normal.cn: 病毒不是细胞，因此病毒学处在生物学边缘，并常与免疫学合作。

abstract.en: Picture a sealed box where a thing smaller than light is grown on purpose.
abstract.cn: 想象一个密封箱，里面故意培养着一种比光波长还小的东西。

abstract.en: Picture a genome printed as letters on a screen, and a scientist reading it like a map.
abstract.cn: 想象一份基因组像字母一样印在屏幕上，科学家像读地图一样读它。

abstract.en: Picture a bat colony and a hospital ward linked by one line on a map.
abstract.cn: 想象地图上一条线，把一个蝙蝠群落和一间医院病房连起来。

examples.en: Virology has identified the family to which the new agent belongs.
examples.cn: 病毒学已经鉴定出这种新因子所属的科。

examples.en: She moved from clinical medicine into virology.
examples.cn: 她从临床医学转入病毒学。

examples.en: Molecular virology explained why the drug no longer worked.
examples.cn: 分子病毒学解释了为什么这种药不再有效。

dict_mnemonic.text: virus（病毒）+ -logy（……学）→ 研究病毒的学科 → virology 病毒学

root: 拉丁 virus「毒、黏液」→ 英语 virus；希腊 -logia「研究、论述」→ -logy；1935 年英语合成 virus + -logy = virology；virologist 出现于 1946 年。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the science itself to its institution, clinical, molecular, diagnostic, botanical and practical branches, and finally to its metonymic use for a sample's viral content.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从这门科学本身，走向它的建制、临床、分子、诊断、植物与实践分支，最后落到用学科名转指样本中的病毒组成。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sealed cabinet and a genome on screen, with a sample log beside them.
core.cn: 核心意象：密封操作箱与屏幕上的基因组，旁边放着样本记录。

branches.en: KNOWLEDGE: the organised study of viruses is the root sense.
branches.cn: 知识：对病毒的系统研究是根义。

branches.en: INSTITUTION: a department with a building makes the field visible as an organisation.
branches.cn: 建制：有楼有人的院系让这个领域作为组织变得可见。

branches.en: CLINICAL PATH: the clinic identifies the agent, and diagnostics types it for treatment.
branches.cn: 临床路径：诊所鉴定因子，诊断部门为治疗而分型。

branches.en: MECHANISM AND HANDS: molecular work explains entry and copying, while laboratory methods make the work safe.
branches.cn: 机制与双手：分子工作解释进入与复制，实验室方法让工作安全。

branches.en: WIDER OBJECT: plants and ecosystems are studied too, and 'the virology of a sample' is the object standing in for the field.
branches.cn: 更宽的对象：植物与生态系统也在研究之列，而「样本的病毒学」是对象代学科出场。

intro.en: Virology is two elements: a Latin noun for poison and a Greek suffix for study, joined in English in the twentieth century.
intro.cn: virology 由两个成分构成：表示「毒」的拉丁名词与表示「研究」的希腊后缀，二十世纪在英语中组合。

latinIntro.en: Latin gave virus; Greek gave -logia through Latin -logia. The compound is modern, so there is no single classical Latin word behind it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了 virus，希腊语经拉丁 -logia 提供了后缀；这个复合词是现代的，因此背后没有单一的古典拉丁词。

definition_zh: 使成团；聚集；团块；结块的
definition_en: to gather into a mass or cluster; a clustered mass; formed into a ball or heap
core_image: 滚雪球：碎屑越滚越大，粘成一团
scene: 山脚下，火山灰凝成了拳头大的石块。 Ash fragments agglomerate into round stones as the volcano cools.
sceneCN: 这里 agglomerate 是「聚结成团」（第 1 个义项：散粒黏聚为一体）；句意是火山冷却时，灰烬碎屑聚结成圆石。

derivatives.zh: agglomerate 加名词后缀 -ion，义为「聚集（体）；集结」
同根拉丁 glomus 一支，义为「小球状聚伞花序」
同根加 con- 前缀，义为「混合聚集物；企业集团」

senses.title: To collect or form into a mass or ball
senses.definition: to gather scattered particles or things into one clustered mass
senses.definitionCN: 把分散的颗粒或事物黏聚成一个团块
senses.example: Ash fragments agglomerate into round stones as the volcano cools.
senses.exampleCN: 火山冷却时，灰烬碎屑聚结成圆石。
senses.why: The Latin root glomus means a ball of yarn; rolling loose threads into a ball is the exact image of gathering particles into a lump.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 glomus 意为「线团」；把散线滚成球，正是「碎粒聚成团块」的核心画面。

senses.title: A clustered mass, especially of rock or businesses
senses.definition: a mass of clustered fragments, or a group of firms or districts grown together
senses.definitionCN: 碎块聚成的团，或连成一片的企业群、城镇群
senses.example: The firm grew from a workshop into an agglomerate of fourteen brands.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司从一间作坊成长为拥有十四个品牌的联合体。
senses.why: Whatever particles do, institutions imitate: separate units fused into one body are a ball of yarn in the economic image.
senses.whyCN: 颗粒会成团，机构亦然：各自独立却熔为一体的单位，在经济图景里就是一个「线团」。

senses.title: Formed into a clustered mass
senses.definition: describing matter that has clumped together rather than staying dispersed
senses.definitionCN: 形容物质已结块抱团，而非保持分散
senses.example: Powder that has absorbed moisture becomes agglomerate and will not pour.
senses.exampleCN: 受潮的粉末会结成团，倒不出来了。
senses.why: The result state of the action becomes a property: once rolled into a ball, the material is simply agglomerate.
senses.whyCN: 动作的结果沉淀为属性：一旦滚成了球，这种材料就「是」结块的了。

intro.en: From Latin agglomerare (to wind into a ball), built on glomus (ball of yarn), through post-classical and scientific Latin into English.
intro.cn: 源自拉丁语 agglomerare「卷成球」，建立在 glomus（线团）之上，经近代学术拉丁语进入英语。

items.en: The root *glem- (to stick, to smear) is reconstructed behind glomus and its cousins.
items.cn: 一般认为 glomus 及其同族词背后是重构词根 *glem-（粘、涂）。

items.en: glomus meant a ball of yarn; agglomerare meant to add to the ball, to wind on.
items.cn: 拉丁语 glomus 意为「线团」，agglomerare 意为「往球上绕、卷成一团」。

items.en: agglomeratus served in alchemy and early geology for fused lumps of matter.
items.cn: 近代拉丁语 agglomeratus 用于炼金术与早期地质学，指熔结的块状物。

items.en: Science adopted the verb for particles clustering, later for rocks and city growth.
items.cn: 十七至十九世纪科学界用其动词指颗粒结团，后扩展到岩石与城市扩张。

items.en: Today the word lives in geology, materials science, and economics of urban clusters.
items.cn: 如今该词活跃于地质学、材料科学和城市经济学的「集聚」语境。

note.en: Agglomerate stresses one coherent ball; agglomeration is looser, and conglomeration implies a mixed heap.
note.cn: agglomerate 强调凝成一个整体；agglomeration 较松散，conglomeration 则含「混杂堆聚」之意。
