definition_zh: 不公正；不公平；不义之举；冤屈；制度性的不公
definition_en: the absence of even-handedness, and any act or arrangement that gives one party less than its due
core_image: 村口的木秤被人偷偷在一端灌了铅，秤砣还没挪动，低下去的那一头就已经判定了输赢
scene: 集市上有人发现那杆秤的一头被灌了铅，买粮的农妇还没开口，围观的人已经替她不平。 The crowd protested against the injustice of a scale that had been weighted before anyone weighed.
sceneCN: 这里指「称量被暗中做了手脚」的不公，对应第 1 个义项：本该用同一把尺子，却有人事先偏了心；句意为众人抗议一杆事先被加重过的秤所造成的不公。画面要点：被灌铅的木秤、围拢的集市人群。

pos.zh: 不公正；不公平（不可数，指性质）
不义之举；冤屈（可数，指一桩具体的事）

forms.label: 不可数名词（不公的性质）

derivatives.zh: 去掉名词后缀，换形容词词尾（源自拉丁语 iustus）→ 由「不公之事」转为「不公正的」
unjust 加副词后缀（古英语中表方式）→ 由「不公正的」转为「以不公的方式」
加复数后缀 → 由「一桩不义之举」转为「多桩不义之举」
去掉否定前缀（拉丁语中表否定）→ 由「不公」反转为「公正」

senses.title: Absence of even-handedness
senses.definition: the failure to apply one and the same rule to all parties concerned
senses.definitionCN: 未能对相关各方适用同一套规则
senses.example: The parents complained of injustice when only one child was punished.
senses.exampleCN: 只有一个孩子受到惩罚，父母便抱怨这不公平。
senses.why: The core image is a beam secretly loaded at one end: before any weighing begins the measure already favours a side, and that prior tilt is the first sense.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是一根被人在一端偷偷加重的秤梁：还没开始称，尺子就已经偏向一边；这个事先的倾斜就是第一个义项。

senses.title: A single unjust deed
senses.definition: one act that takes from someone what is owed to them
senses.definitionCN: 夺走某人应得之物的某一个行为
senses.example: The seizure of the family's land was an injustice no court would defend.
senses.exampleCN: 没收这家人土地是一桩没有哪家法院愿意为之辩护的不义之举。
senses.why: A tilted beam produces a reading; written into an act, that reading becomes a deed with a victim, and the abstract failure hardens into something countable.
senses.whyCN: 倾斜的秤梁给出一个读数；把它写成一个行为，这个读数就成了带有受害者的举动，抽象的性质凝结为可数的一件事。

senses.title: Wrongful handling by courts or officials
senses.titleCN: 法院或官员的错误处置
senses.definition: the mishandling of a case, especially a conviction or ruling that the person does not deserve
senses.definitionCN: 对案件的不当处置，尤指当事人不应得的定罪或裁决
senses.example: The inquiry found injustice in the way the confession had been obtained.
senses.exampleCN: 调查认定，取得那份口供的方式存在不公。
senses.why: Because the balance is most visible in a courtroom, its crooked version is most often charged against courts: the institution meant to hold it level is accused of holding it wrong.
senses.whyCN: 天平在法庭里最显眼，所以它歪掉的样子最常被算在法院头上：本该把秤端平的机关，被指为把秤端歪了。

senses.title: Unfairness built into the rules
senses.titleCN: 写进规则里的结构性不公
senses.definition: unfairness built into the rules of a society, market or institution, so that some groups are always short-changed
senses.definitionCN: 社会、市场或机构规则中固有的不公，使某些群体总是吃亏
senses.example: Campaigners described the tax as a quiet injustice written into the code.
senses.exampleCN: 活动人士把这项税称为悄悄写进法规的一处不公。
senses.why: One loaded pan can be a mistake; the same load placed in every scale of a country becomes a structure, and the word moves from an event to the order of things.
senses.whyCN: 一只托盘被加重可以是失误；把同样的加重放进一国的每一杆秤，就成了结构，这个词也从一件事移到事物的秩序上。

senses.title: A wrong a person has suffered
senses.definition: the grievance or injury that a person carries after being treated unfairly
senses.definitionCN: 一个人受到不公对待之后背负的委屈或伤害
senses.example: She never spoke of the injustice she had suffered at the factory.
senses.exampleCN: 她从不谈起自己在厂里受过的冤屈。
senses.why: Every tilted reading leaves a weight in the lighter pan; that residue, felt by the person, is the wrong carried rather than the act that caused it.
senses.whyCN: 每一次倾斜的称量都在较轻的那只托盘里留下重量；这份被当事人感到的残余，是背在身上的冤屈，而不是造成它的那个行为。

senses.title: An unfair verdict on a person
senses.definition: an unjust judgement of someone's character, work or worth
senses.definitionCN: 对某人的品性、工作或价值所作的不公正评判
senses.example: To call him lazy would do him an injustice.
senses.exampleCN: 说他懒，那对他就太不公平了。
senses.why: The scale can be turned on a reputation instead of a purse: weighing a person by false evidence is the same crooked operation in miniature.
senses.whyCN: 天平可以对着名声而不是对着钱袋：用不实的证据去称一个人，是同一套歪掉的把戏，只是缩小了规模。

senses.title: An unreasonable burden laid on one side
senses.titleCN: 单方面压下的不合理负担
senses.definition: a demand or condition that places more on one party than fairness allows
senses.definitionCN: 把超出公平限度之多的东西压到某一方头上的要求或条件
senses.example: The new levy placed an injustice on small shops that could least afford it.
senses.exampleCN: 新征的费用把一重不合理的负担压在最无力承担的小店铺身上。
senses.why: If the load is put on only one pan before weighing starts, the demand is already decided; the word then names the pre-loaded burden rather than the deed that follows.
senses.whyCN: 如果在称量开始前就把重量只压在一只托盘上，要求其实已经定了；此时这个词指那份额外压上的负担，而不是随后的行为。

senses.title: The unfairness of chance
senses.definition: the unjust character of fate, fortune or natural events, which distribute good and ill without regard to merit
senses.definitionCN: 命运、运气或自然事件的不义性质：它们不分功过地分发好坏
senses.example: They spoke of the injustice of a storm that spared the warehouse and ruined the homes.
senses.exampleCN: 他们说起那场风暴的不公：它放过了仓库，却毁掉了住宅。
senses.why: The beam is now held by no visible hand; when no one can be blamed, the word still names the tilt, and injustice becomes the shape of chance itself.
senses.whyCN: 此时秤梁没有看得见的手在握；当无人可以归咎时，这个词仍指那道倾斜，不公于是成了运气本身的形状。

intro.en: Injustice is the negative of justice: Latin in- 'not' was added to iustitia, and Latin already had injustitia and injustus. Old French carried the form on, and English borrowed it with the negative prefix intact.
intro.cn: injustice 是 justice 的否定形式：拉丁否定前缀加在 iustitia 之上，而拉丁本身已有 injustitia 与 injustus。古法语把这个形式传下去，英语带着完整否定前缀借入。

items.en: Latin in- marked negation, and its shape could change before certain consonants; on a noun of quality it produced the opposite quality.
items.cn: 拉丁语中表否定的前缀，在部分辅音前形态会有变化；加在表性质的名词上，就造出相反的性质。

items.en: Iustitia 'justice' was the abstract noun of iustus 'just', itself built on ius 'right, law'.
items.cn: iustitia「公正」是 iustus「公正的」的抽象名词，而 iustus 又立在 ius「法权、法律」之上。

items.en: Latin formed iniustitia 'injustice' directly, and the adjective iniustus 'unjust' already existed beside it.
items.cn: 拉丁直接造出了 iniustitia「不公」，与之并存的形容词 iniustus「不公正的」也已经存在。

items.en: Old French used injustice for both the quality and a wrong done; the exact century of the borrowing into English is uncertain.
items.cn: 古法语用 injustice 兼指这种性质与一桩不义之事；借入英语的确切世纪不确定。

items.en: English records the word early but the precise first date is uncertain; it named the quality first and a countable act later.
items.cn: 英语早期文献已见该词，但确切首见年代不确定；它先指性质，后指可数的一桩事。

note.en: The first group keeps the ius root in other shapes; the second group gives near alternatives, one of which comes from a different root and must not be confused with this family.
note.cn: 第一组以别的形态保留 ius 词根；第二组是近义替代，其中一个出自另一条词根，不能与这一族混为一谈。

entries.definition: Not fair or lawful; it is the negative of just and states the quality where injustice states the thing.
entries.definitionCN: 不公的、不合法的；它是否定形式的「公正的」，说的是性质，而不公说的是事情本身。

entries.definition: To harm a person physically; it comes from Latin injuria 'wrong' but has narrowed from injustice to bodily damage.
entries.definitionCN: 在身体上伤害人；出自拉丁 injuria「不义」，但语义已从「不公」收窄为「身体损伤」。

entries.definition: Harmful or wrongful; the same family as injure and justice, now used chiefly of damage.
entries.definitionCN: 有害的、造成侵害的；与 injure、justice 同族，现在主要用于损害之义。

entries.definition: Wicked or grossly unfair; it shares the negative prefix but comes from Latin iniquus 'unequal', so it only looks related and is not the same root.
entries.definitionCN: 邪恶的、极不公的；它只共享否定前缀，出自拉丁 iniquus「不均等」，所以只是形近，并非同源。

entries.definition: The plain everyday name for the same failure; it comes from Old English fæger and is unrelated to the Latin root of injustice.
entries.definitionCN: 同一种缺失最平实的说法；它出自古英语 fæger，与 injustice 的拉丁词根没有源流关系。

entries.definition: An act or state that violates what is right; it does not require a rule or a comparison of parties.
entries.definitionCN: 违反正当之事的举动或状态；它不要求有规则，也不要求比较双方。

entries.definition: Lack of evenness in treatment, from Latin aequus 'even'; the root is different from ius, though the effect described is close.
entries.definitionCN: 待遇上的不均等，出自拉丁 aequus「平坦、均等」；词根与 ius 不同，尽管所描述的效果相近。

entries.definition: Unfairness held in place by power, so that the weaker side cannot appeal; it adds force to the idea of injustice.
entries.definitionCN: 以权力维持的不公，使较弱一方无从申诉；它在「不公」之上加了强制这一层。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the negative prefix, the real family words and the real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的否定前缀、真实的同族词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: In- is the plain Latin 'not', so injustice is justice with that switch thrown.
normal.cn: 这个否定前缀就是拉丁语里平实的「不」，所以 injustice 是把 justice 的那个开关扳到否定。

normal.en: Unjust and unjustly carry the same switch into the adjective and the adverb.
normal.cn: unjust 与 unjustly 把同一个否定开关带进了形容词和副词。

normal.en: The noun turns countable when it names one deed: an injustice, two injustices.
normal.cn: 当它指一桩具体的事，这个名词就可数：一桩不义之举、两桩不义之举。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: do someone an injustice, redress an injustice, social injustice.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：冤枉某人、纠正一桩不公、社会不公。

normal.en: The root line is shared with justice: ius 'right', iustus 'just', iustitia 'justice'.
normal.cn: 词根线与 justice 共享：ius「法权」、iustus「公正的」、iustitia「公正」。

abstract.en: Picture one pan of a balance with a lump of lead hidden under it, the beam already down before the goods arrive.
abstract.cn: 想象天平的一只托盘底下藏着一块铅，货物还没放上去，秤梁已经先沉了下去。

abstract.en: Picture a ruler with the first inch filed away, so that every honest measurement comes out short.
abstract.cn: 想象一把尺子的第一寸被锉掉了，于是每一次老实的测量都偏短。

abstract.en: Picture a race where one lane's starting line is chalked several steps behind the others.
abstract.cn: 想象一场赛跑，其中一条跑道的起跑线被画在别人后面好几步的地方。

examples.en: The report catalogued a long history of injustice against the fishing villages.
examples.cn: 报告记录了这些渔村长期遭受不公的历史。

examples.en: He considered it an injustice that the oldest workers were the first to be dismissed.
examples.cn: 他认为最先被辞退的是最年长的工人，这实在不公。

examples.en: No apology can undo the injustice of those lost years.
examples.cn: 任何道歉都无法抹去那些失去的年岁所造成的不公。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因贾斯蒂斯」——把开头记成「因为」：因为有人偷偷往秤里加了分量，斯文的天平就歪了 → 不公、不义、冤枉

root: 表否定的拉丁前缀 + justice（拉丁 iustitia，出自 ius「法权」）→ 不公；拉丁已有 iniustitia，经古法语 injustice 进入英语，与 justice 同一词根而意义相反。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all start from one crooked reading: a beam loaded before the weighing. That tilt becomes unfair treatment, then a countable deed, then courts that handle a case wrongly, then rules that load every scale the same way. From there it moves to the wound a person carries, a false verdict on a reputation, a burden laid on one side, and finally a tilt with no hand behind it.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都从同一个歪掉的读数开始：秤在称量之前就被加重。这道倾斜成为不公平的对待，继而成为一桩可数的事、把案子办错的法院、以同样方式给每一杆秤加重的规则；由此再移到当事人背负的伤口、对名声的错判、单方压下的负担，最后是一道找不到推手可归的倾斜。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a beam already loaded at one end, so the result is settled before the weighing.
core.cn: 核心意象：秤梁的一端早已被加重，结果在称量之前就定了。

branches.en: THE TILT ITSELF: one rule fails to reach all parties equally.
branches.cn: 倾斜本身：同一套规则没能同等落到每一方身上。

branches.en: THE DEED: the tilt written into one act that takes what was owed.
branches.cn: 一桩事：把倾斜写进一个行为，夺走本该属于他人的东西。

branches.en: COURTS AND WOUNDS: the crooked reading charged against a court, and the weight it leaves in the victim's pan.
branches.cn: 法院与伤口：把歪掉的读数算在法院头上，以及它留在受害者托盘里的那份重量。

branches.en: STRUCTURE: the same hidden load placed in every scale of a society.
branches.cn: 结构：把同样的暗载放进一个社会的每一杆秤。

branches.en: JUDGEMENT, BURDEN AND FATE: a person weighed falsely, a load pushed onto one side, and a tilt with no hand behind it.
branches.cn: 评判、负担与命运：被不实称量的人、被推到一方头上的重量，以及找不到推手的倾斜。

intro.en: Injustice is a negated Latin abstract noun; the prefix and the noun each keep their own meaning, and the pair travelled together through French.
intro.cn: injustice 是一个被否定的拉丁抽象名词；前缀与名词各自保留自己的意思，二者一起经法语传来。

latinIntro.en: Latin in- 'not' joins iustitia 'justice' to give injustitia; the same negative also produced injustus 'unjust', the adjective that English keeps as unjust.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语表「不」的否定前缀与 iustitia「公正」合起来得到 injustitia；同一个否定成分还造出 injustus「不公正的」，英语把它保留为 unjust。

items.example: In- turns a quality into its absence.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把一种性质变成它的缺失。

items.example: Iustitia is the noun that in- negates.
items.exampleCN: iustitia 正是那个被否定的名词。

items.example: Latin injustitia is the direct model of the English word.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁 injustitia 是英语这个词的直接范本。

items.example: Injustus stands beside injustitia in Latin.
items.exampleCN: 在拉丁语里，injustus 与 injustitia 并立。

items.meaning: the quality of giving each its due
items.meaningCN: 给每一方应得之份的性质
items.example: Without the negative prefix the word means justice.
items.exampleCN: 去掉否定前缀，这个词就是「公正」。

items.example: The crowd protested against the injustice of the scale.
items.exampleCN: 众人抗议那杆秤带来的不公。

items.example: The rules were unjust to the smallest traders.
items.exampleCN: 这些规则对最小的商户并不公平。

items.example: The book lists the injustices of that decade.
items.exampleCN: 这本书列举了那个年代的种种不义之举。

items.example: He was unjustly blamed for the failure.
items.exampleCN: 那次失败他被不公平地归咎了。

definition_zh: 阉公牛；耕牛；牛（通称）
definition_en: a castrated adult male bovine used for draught; a bovine animal in compounds
core_image: 两头阉公牛并排套在木轭上，肩背隆起，拉着犁在硬土里前进
scene: 两头阉公牛并排套进木轭，肩峰顶住横木，犁铧在硬土里翻出连续的土块。 The ox team pulled the plough to the field's far edge.
sceneCN: 这里指「套轭耕田的阉公牛」（第 1 个义项：役用阉公牛）；句意为这对耕牛把犁拉到田的最远端。

derivatives.zh: ox + -en（古英语复数词尾）→ 阉公牛的复数（语义偏移：保留强变化复数）
ox + herd（牧人）→ 牧牛人
ox + cart（车）→ 牛车
ox + bow（弯木）→ 牛轭弯木；河曲（语义偏移：指形似牛轭的河湾）
ox + hide（皮）→ 牛皮
ox + eye（眼）→ 牛眼菊（语义偏移：指花盘像牛眼的花）
ox + blood（血）→ 深红色（语义偏移：指像牛血的颜色）

senses.title: A castrated adult male bovine
senses.definition: an adult male bovine that has been castrated, usually for work
senses.definitionCN: 已阉割的成年公牛，通常用于劳作
senses.example: The ox was quieter than the bull beside it.
senses.exampleCN: 这头阉牛比旁边的公牛安静。
senses.why: The core sense is a sex-and-work class, not simply a male bovine.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是一个性别与劳作等级，而非单纯的雄性牛。

senses.title: A draught animal in a team
senses.definition: an ox trained to pull a plough, cart or load, usually paired with another
senses.definitionCN: 受训拉犁、拉车或拉货的牛，通常与另一头配对
senses.example: The team of oxen turned the heavy soil in long lines.
senses.exampleCN: 这对耕牛拉着长线翻动重土。
senses.why: Castration made the animal tractable, so work is the reason the class exists.
senses.whyCN: 阉割使动物温顺，因此劳作是这个等级存在的理由。

senses.title: A bovine in compounds
senses.definition: a general bovine reference in compounds such as oxhide, ox tongue or ox-eye
senses.definitionCN: 在 oxhide、ox tongue、ox-eye 等复合词中泛指牛
senses.example: The drum was stretched with oxhide.
senses.exampleCN: 这面鼓用牛皮蒙成。
senses.why: In compounds the sex distinction fades, and ox becomes a plain word for the animal's body or products.
senses.whyCN: 在复合词中性别区分淡化，ox 变成指动物身体或产物的普通词。

senses.title: Ox meat and parts
senses.definition: the meat or edible parts of an ox, as in ox tongue or ox cheek
senses.definitionCN: 阉牛的肉或可食部位，如牛舌、牛颊
senses.example: The ox tongue was boiled with herbs.
senses.exampleCN: 牛舌与香草一起煮。
senses.why: The working animal also enters the kitchen, and its name survives on cuts and dishes.
senses.whyCN: 役用动物也进入厨房，其名留在肉块与菜肴上。

senses.title: The zodiac Ox
senses.definition: the second sign of the Chinese zodiac, rendered in English as the Ox
senses.definitionCN: 中国生肖的第二位，英语译作 the Ox
senses.example: The Year of the Ox began with the new moon.
senses.exampleCN: 牛年随新月开始。
senses.why: Translation chose the farm ox as the English name for a zodiac branch, and the image stuck.
senses.whyCN: 翻译选用农家的牛作为某个生肖地支的英语名，这个意象固定下来。

senses.title: A very strong person
senses.definition: a person compared to an ox for strength or patient endurance
senses.definitionCN: 因力量或耐性而被比作牛的人
senses.example: He was strong as an ox and just as silent.
senses.exampleCN: 他力大如牛，也一样沉默。
senses.why: The ox's strength and patience, not its intellect, supply the comparison.
senses.whyCN: 提供比较的是牛的力气与耐性，而非智力。

senses.title: A yoke as a pair
senses.definition: a pair of oxen joined by one yoke, treated as a working unit
senses.definitionCN: 由同一副轭连成一对、作为一个劳作单位的牛
senses.example: A yoke of oxen could plough an acre in a day.
senses.exampleCN: 一对同轭耕牛一天能犁一英亩。
senses.why: The harness, not the animal, becomes the unit, and English counts ploughing by the yoke.
senses.whyCN: 成为单位的是轭具而非动物，英语按「轭」计算犁地。

senses.title: A sacrificial animal
senses.definition: an ox offered in classical or biblical sacrifice
senses.definitionCN: 在古典或圣经祭祀中献上的牛
senses.example: The temple accepted a perfect ox without blemish.
senses.exampleCN: 神庙接受一头无瑕的牛。
senses.why: The ox was the costliest common sacrificial animal, which is why the word appears in ritual law.
senses.whyCN: 牛是最昂贵的常见祭牲，因此这个词出现在祭祀律法中。

intro.en: Ox goes back to Old English oxa, from Proto-Germanic uhsō(n), from an Indo-European word for ox or bull. The plural oxen preserves an old strong ending. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: ox 可上溯到古英语 oxa，来自原始日耳曼语 uhsō(n)，再上溯一个表示牛或公牛的印欧词。复数 oxen 保留古老强变化词尾。年代均为约数。

items.en: Oxa named the castrated male bovine, and the plural oxan already showed the old ending.
items.cn: oxa 指阉割的雄性牛，复数 oxan 已显示古老词尾。

items.en: The Germanic form is reconstructed from English, German and Old Norse evidence.
items.cn: 这个日耳曼形式是由英语、德语与古诺斯语证据重构的。

items.en: The root behind ox is a separate bovine word from the root that gives Latin bos and Greek bous, so the two families are not close relatives.
items.cn: ox 背后的词根与给出拉丁 bos、希腊 bous 的词根属于不同的「牛」词，因此两个词族并非近亲。

items.en: The plural oxen keeps a strong noun ending that most English nouns have lost, which is why the form looks irregular.
items.cn: 复数 oxen 保留多数英语名词已丢失的强变化词尾，因此这个形式看起来不规则。

items.en: The animal's role as a plough team and as a sacrifice gave English the phrases a yoke of oxen and the sacrificial ox.
items.cn: 这种动物作为犁队与祭牲的角色，给英语留下「一轭牛」与「祭牛」的说法。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper root): the Indo-European form is reconstructed, and its relation to the other bovine roots is not settled.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词根）：印欧形式属重构，它与其他「牛」词根的关系尚未定论。

note.en: Group one holds ox compounds that are easily mistaken for the animal; group two holds the separate words for bovine age, sex and use.
note.cn: 第一组是由 ox 构成、易被误当成动物本身的复合词；第二组是按年龄、性别与用途区分牛的独立词。

entries.definition: The U-shaped collar of an ox yoke, or a river bend of that shape; it is not an animal.
entries.definitionCN: 牛轭的 U 形弯木，或形似它的河湾；它不是动物。

entries.definition: A daisy-like flower with a large yellow centre, named for its ox-eye look; it is a plant.
entries.definitionCN: 花盘大而黄、形似牛眼的花；它是植物。

entries.definition: A cart pulled by oxen; it names the vehicle, not the team.
entries.definitionCN: 由牛拉的车；它命名车辆，不是牛队。

entries.definition: A person who tends oxen; it is the keeper, not the animal.
entries.definitionCN: 照看牛的人；它是看守者，不是动物。

entries.definition: An adult uncastrated male bovine; an ox is a bull that has been castrated for work.
entries.definitionCN: 成年未阉割的公牛；ox 是已为劳作而阉割的公牛。

entries.definition: A young castrated male bovine, often raised for beef; ox is usually older and trained to work.
entries.definitionCN: 年轻的阉公牛，常为肉用；ox 通常更年长且受训劳作。

entries.definition: A young bull or a castrated bull, especially in British regional use; it overlaps with ox but is usually younger.
entries.definitionCN: 年轻公牛或阉公牛，尤见于英国方言；与 ox 重叠，但通常更年轻。

entries.definition: Bovines as a group; ox names one castrated working animal within the herd.
entries.definitionCN: 作为整体的牛；ox 指牛群中一头阉割的役用牛。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Old English oxa and the old plural oxan explain the irregular oxen.
normal.cn: 古英语 oxa 与旧复数 oxan 解释了不规则的 oxen。

normal.en: The family runs ox, oxen, oxherd, oxcart, oxbow, oxhide, oxeye.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 ox、oxen、oxherd、oxcart、oxbow、oxhide、oxeye。

normal.en: Fixed phrases split the uses: a yoke of oxen, ox cart, ox hide.
normal.cn: 固定搭配区分用法：一对同轭牛、牛车、牛皮。

normal.en: Ox is a castrated bull, not any bull; the knife made it workable.
normal.cn: ox 是阉过的公牛，不是任何公牛；是刀使它可用。

normal.en: The zodiac Ox is a translation choice, not a biological category.
normal.cn: 生肖牛是翻译选择，不是生物学类别。

abstract.en: Picture two heavy bodies joined by one wooden bar, moving as a single machine.
abstract.cn: 想象两具沉重的身体被一根木杠连成一台机器。

abstract.en: Picture a river bending back on itself like a yoke left in the grass.
abstract.cn: 想象一条河弯回自身，像遗在草里的牛轭。

abstract.en: Picture a silent man carrying what four others cannot lift.
abstract.cn: 想象一个沉默的人扛起四个人抬不动的东西。

examples.en: A yoke of oxen pulled the stone boat.
examples.cn: 一对同轭耕牛拉着石船。

examples.en: The oxen were fed before the people.
examples.cn: 先喂牛，再喂人。

examples.en: He was strong as an ox but slow to anger.
examples.cn: 他力大如牛，却不易发怒。

dict_mnemonic.text: ox 是阉过的成年公牛，复数 oxen；套上轭就是耕牛，因此有 a yoke of oxen；牛皮、牛舌、牛眼菊都用它作限定成分。

root: 古英语 oxa「阉公牛」→ 原始日耳曼 uhsō(n) → 印欧牛词；复数 oxen 保留古强变化词尾。该词根与拉丁 bos、希腊 bous 不同源，更早形式属重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one working animal: the castrated male, the draught team, the generic bovine, meat, the zodiac, strength, the yoke as a unit and the sacrifice.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一头役用动物展开：阉公牛、役畜队、泛指牛、牛肉、生肖、力气、以轭为单位与祭牲。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a heavy animal stands under a wooden yoke, and the yoke turns it into a unit of power.
core.cn: 核心意象：一头沉重的动物站在木轭下，木轭把它变成一单位动力。

branches.en: THE ANIMAL: castration defines the class before any work begins.
branches.cn: 动物：在开始任何劳作之前，阉割先定义了等级。

branches.en: THE TEAM: the pair under one yoke is the ploughing unit.
branches.cn: 牛队：同轭的一对是犁地单位。

branches.en: THE BODY: in compounds and in the kitchen, ox becomes plain bovine flesh.
branches.cn: 身体：在复合词与厨房里，ox 变成普通的牛肉与牛身。

branches.en: THE ZODIAC: translation turns the farm animal into a calendar sign.
branches.cn: 生肖：翻译把农场动物变成历法符号。

branches.en: STRENGTH AND SACRIFICE: the same body is admired for power and offered in ritual.
branches.cn: 力气与祭祀：同一具身体既因力量被赞叹，也在仪式中被献上。

intro.en: Ox is a native Germanic noun with an old irregular plural; its family is built by compounding, not by Latin suffixes.
intro.cn: ox 是日耳曼本族名词，带一个古老的不规则复数；其词族靠复合而非拉丁后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin relative exists for ox, since Latin bos and Greek bous belong to a different bovine root, so the Latin side is left empty.
latinIntro.cn: ox 没有可靠的拉丁同族词，因为拉丁 bos 与希腊 bous 属于另一「牛」词根，所以拉丁部分留空。

items.example: The Old English noun already meant the working animal.
items.exampleCN: 这个古英语名词已指役用动物。

items.example: The ending survives only in a few nouns such as oxen.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾只保留在少数名词中，如 oxen。

items.structure: ox (English noun, from Old English oxa)
items.example: The ox pulled the cart without complaint.
items.exampleCN: 这头牛毫无怨言地拉车。

items.example: The oxen were yoked before dawn.
items.exampleCN: 牛在天亮前被套上轭。

items.example: The oxherd slept beside the stall.
items.exampleCN: 牧牛人睡在牛栏旁。

items.example: The oxcart carried the harvest home.
items.exampleCN: 牛车把收成运回家。

items.meaning: a yoke's U-shaped collar; a river bend
items.example: The river left an oxbow in the meadow.
items.exampleCN: 河在草地上留下一个牛轭弯。

items.example: The shield was covered with oxhide.
items.exampleCN: 盾面蒙着牛皮。

items.example: Oxeye daisies filled the verge.
items.exampleCN: 牛眼菊长满了路旁。

definition_zh: 潮湿的；湿润的；闷热的（空气或天气）
definition_en: containing a lot of water vapour; damp and often uncomfortably warm
core_image: 热带雨季的午后，墙壁摸上去发潮，风扇吹来的风也是热的
scene: 热带雨季的午后，墙壁摸上去发潮，风扇吹来的风带着热气。 The air felt humid even in the shade of the veranda.
sceneCN: 这里 humid 指「空气含水汽多、潮湿的」（第 1 个义项：空气潮湿的）；句意为即使站在走廊的阴凉处，空气仍然潮湿。图中可辨识物件：潮湿的墙、风扇、走廊阴影、水汽。

derivatives.zh: 湿度；潮湿
潮湿地（罕用）
潮湿性（罕用）
加湿；使湿润
除湿

senses.title: Damp air
senses.definition: describing air that holds a great deal of water vapour
senses.definitionCN: 形容空气含有大量水汽
senses.example: The air felt humid even in the shade of the veranda.
senses.exampleCN: 即使站在走廊的阴凉处，空气仍然潮湿。
senses.why: Latin humidus simply meant moist, and English kept that plain physical sense first.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 humidus 本义就是潮湿，英语最先保留了这个朴素的物理义。

senses.title: A wet climate
senses.definition: describing a region or season with high moisture and frequent rain
senses.definitionCN: 形容一个地区或季节水汽高、降雨频繁
senses.example: Rice grows well in a humid climate.
senses.exampleCN: 水稻在湿润的气候里长得好。
senses.why: a region's moisture is what makes a climate humid, not a single day.
senses.whyCN: 使气候算得上湿润的是一个地区的水汽，而不是某一天。

senses.title: Oppressively warm and damp
senses.definition: describing warmth made worse by moisture, so that the body cannot cool
senses.definitionCN: 形容潮湿使炎热更难忍受，身体无法散热
senses.example: The humid heat kept everyone indoors at noon.
senses.exampleCN: 湿热的暑气让正午时人人都待在室内。
senses.why: moisture slows evaporation, and the word absorbed that discomfort.
senses.whyCN: 水汽减慢蒸发，这个词就吸收了这种不适。

senses.title: A moist air mass
senses.titleCN: 气象学上含大量水汽的气团
senses.definition: technical: describing an air mass whose vapour content is high
senses.definitionCN: 技术用法：形容水汽含量高的气团
senses.example: A humid air mass from the sea met a cold front inland.
senses.exampleCN: 来自海上的湿气团在内陆遇上冷锋。
senses.why: meteorology needs a label for vapour-rich air, and the adjective serves it.
senses.whyCN: 气象学需要给富含水汽的空气一个标签，这个形容词就服务于此。

senses.title: A damp room
senses.definition: describing a room, wall or building that feels or stays wet
senses.definitionCN: 形容房间、墙壁或建筑摸上去或一直是湿的
senses.example: The humid cellar smelled of old stone.
senses.exampleCN: 潮湿的地窖散发着旧石头的味道。
senses.why: a room that stays wet earns the adjective just as air does.
senses.whyCN: 一直湿着的房间也像空气一样配得上这个形容词。

senses.title: A moist habitat
senses.definition: describing an environment wet enough for moisture-loving plants and animals
senses.definitionCN: 形容环境足够湿润，适合喜湿的动植物
senses.example: Ferns cover the humid slopes above the stream.
senses.exampleCN: 蕨类铺满溪流上方湿润的坡地。
senses.why: plants that need moisture mark their habitats with the word.
senses.whyCN: 需要水汽的植物用这个词来标记它们的栖息地。

senses.title: Causing dampness
senses.definition: describing conditions that make objects, clothes or food damp
senses.definitionCN: 形容使物品、衣物或食物受潮的状况
senses.example: The humid weather left the salt in lumps.
senses.exampleCN: 潮湿的天气让盐结成了块。
senses.why: if the air will not take more water, objects keep the damp.
senses.whyCN: 如果空气不再收水，物品就把潮湿留住。

senses.title: The feel of a wet season
senses.definition: describing the characteristic air of a rainy season
senses.definitionCN: 形容雨季特有的空气感
senses.example: Everything in the humid season dries slowly.
senses.exampleCN: 雨季里什么东西都干得慢。
senses.why: a whole season can have a character, and the adjective names it.
senses.whyCN: 整个季节也能有一种性格，这个形容词为它命名。

intro.en: Humid comes from Latin humidus 'moist', an adjective from humere 'to be moist'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: humid 来自拉丁 humidus「潮湿的」，它是 humere「潮湿」的形容词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Humere meant 'to be moist' or 'to be wet'. Its deeper origin is not established; the Indo-European root often cited for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: humere 意为「潮湿、湿」。其更深来源未得到证明，常为它引用的印欧词根属重构形式。

items.en: Humidus 'moist, wet' was formed from humere and existed beside the variant umidus.
items.cn: humidus「潮湿的」由 humere 构成，并与变体 umidus 并存。

items.en: English humid appears in the sixteenth century, borrowed through French, and first described damp air and damp ground.
items.cn: 英语 humid 在十六世纪出现，经法语借入，最初描述潮湿的空气与地面。

items.en: The word settled into weather description, especially for warm air full of vapour.
items.cn: 这个词稳定用于天气描写，尤指饱含水汽的暖空气。

items.en: Meteorology uses it for air masses with high vapour content, and the noun humidity carries the measured value.
items.cn: 气象学用它形容水汽含量高的气团，名词 humidity 则承载测得的数值。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Latin source of humere is not established, and its first English date is approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：humere 在拉丁语之前的来源未得到证明，它在英语中的首见年代也只是约数。

note.en: Group one holds words that look like humid but come from other roots; group two holds adjectives for wetness and sticky heat.
note.cn: 第一组是外形像 humid、却来自其他词根的词；第二组是表示潮湿与湿热黏腻的形容词。

entries.definition: From Latin humilis 'low' and humus 'earth': modesty. It shares letters with humid but not a root.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 humilis「低微的」与 humus「土地」：谦逊。它与 humid 共享字母，却不共词根。

entries.definition: Organic matter in soil, from Latin humus; it is solid earth, not moist air.
entries.definitionCN: 土壤中的有机质，来自拉丁 humus；它是固体泥土，不是潮湿空气。

entries.definition: To make the air moist; it is an action, while humid is a state.
entries.definitionCN: 使空气潮湿；它是动作，而 humid 是状态。

entries.definition: Relating to the four bodily humours of old medicine; the root is humor 'fluid', not humidity.
entries.definitionCN: 与旧医学的四种体液有关；词根是 humor「液体」，不是湿度。

entries.definition: Slightly wet, often in an unpleasant way; humidusually describes air rather than a surface.
entries.definitionCN: 轻微潮湿，常带不快意味；humid 通常描述空气，而非表面。

entries.definition: Slightly wet in a neutral or pleasant way, as cake or eyes; humid is about air.
entries.definitionCN: 中性或宜人的轻微湿润，如蛋糕或眼睛；humid 讲的是空气。

entries.definition: Unpleasantly warm and damp, used of weather; it adds heat to humidity's moisture.
entries.definitionCN: 令人不适的湿热天气；在 humidity 的水汽之上加了热。

entries.definition: Describing air or a surface that feels adhesive because of moisture; it is the body's impression.
entries.definitionCN: 形容空气或表面因水汽而黏手；是身体的感受。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real word parts, real fixed phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin humere 'to be moist' gives humid, humidity, humidify.
normal.cn: 拉丁 humere「潮湿」给出 humid、humidity、humidify。

normal.en: The family runs humid, humidity, humidly, humidness, dehumidify.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 humid、humidity、humidly、humidness、dehumidify。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: humid air, humid climate, hot and humid.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：潮湿的空气、湿润的气候、又热又潮。

normal.en: The trap is humility, from humus 'earth', meaning modesty.
normal.cn: 陷阱是 humility，出自 humus「土地」，意为谦逊。

normal.en: Humid is about air; damp and moist usually describe surfaces.
normal.cn: humid 讲空气；damp 与 moist 通常描述表面。

abstract.en: Picture a wall you touch and find wet in the afternoon.
abstract.cn: 想象午后摸一面墙，手上是湿的。

abstract.en: Picture a fan pushing warm air that never cools the skin.
abstract.cn: 想象风扇吹着暖风，皮肤却始终不凉。

abstract.en: Picture salt in a bowl slowly turning into lumps.
abstract.cn: 想象碗里的盐慢慢结成块。

examples.en: The humid air made the laundry take two days to dry.
examples.cn: 潮湿的空气让洗好的衣物两天才干。

examples.en: Summers here are hot and humid.
examples.cn: 这里的夏天又热又潮湿。

examples.en: Mould grows quickly in humid cellars.
examples.cn: 霉菌在潮湿的地窖里长得很快。

dict_mnemonic.text: humid 就是「潮湿的」，名词是 humidity（湿度）：空气里水汽多，摸上去湿、身上又闷

root: 拉丁 humere「潮湿」→ humidus「潮湿的」→ 经法语进入英语 humid；更深印欧词根属重构形式，来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one kind of air: damp air, a wet climate, oppressive warmth, a moist air mass, a damp room, a wet habitat, conditions that make things damp and the feel of a rainy season.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一种空气展开：潮湿的空气、湿润的气候、闷热难当、潮湿气团、潮湿地窖、湿润栖息地、使物受潮的天气，以及雨季的湿气感。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wall that feels wet under the palm in the afternoon.
core.cn: 核心意象：午后掌心按上去发热发湿的一面墙。

branches.en: THE PHYSICAL AIR: damp air on the skin and a moist air mass on a map.
branches.cn: 物理的空气：皮肤上的潮湿空气与图上的湿气团。

branches.en: THE WET SEASON: climate, oppressive heat and the feel of the rains belong together.
branches.cn: 雨季：气候、湿热与雨季的体感属于一体。

branches.en: THE ROOM: a cellar stays wet because the air will not take the water.
branches.cn: 房间：地窖一直湿着，因为空气不肯收水。

branches.en: THE HABITAT: ferns mark the slopes where moisture stays.
branches.cn: 栖息地：蕨类标记出水汽停留的坡地。

branches.en: THE CONSEQUENCE: salt lumps and laundry hangs in the same weather.
branches.cn: 后果：同一场天气里盐结块、衣物晾不干。

intro.en: Humid is a Latin adjective whose root also builds the noun for the measured quantity and the verbs for adding or removing moisture.
intro.cn: humid 是一个拉丁形容词，其词根还构成表示可测数量的名词，以及加湿与除湿的动词。

latinIntro.en: Latin humere and humidus supply the core; English adds -ity for the noun and the prefix de- for removal.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 humere 与 humidus 提供核心；英语加 -ity 构成名词，加前缀 de- 表示去除。

items.example: The verb names the state.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词指状态。

items.example: The adjective describes the air.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述空气。

items.example: The air felt humid.
items.exampleCN: 空气显得潮湿。

items.meaning: the amount of vapour in the air
items.example: Humidity stayed high.
items.exampleCN: 湿度居高不下。

items.example: The room was humidly warm.
items.exampleCN: 房间潮热。

items.example: Humidness is hard to measure by feel.
